articles.title: Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
articles.summary:
During an hourlong earnings call last night, Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe spent less time talking about the production ramp of the all-important R2 SUV than he did hyping the company’s still-unproven autonomous vehicle ambitions.
Rivian’s autonomy gamble faces its first real test
RJ Scaringe spent nearly half of Rivian’s earnings call hyping self-driving tech. But taking on Tesla’s FSD with custom chips and pricey lidar is an enormous gamble while the mass-market R2 is still scaling up.
But the company faces a crucial test later this year, when it rolls out its point-to-point hands-free driving feature — first to its own employees for testing and validation in 2026, and later to customers in 2027. Following that, Rivian says it will launch its first robotaxi vehicles in partnership with Uber in 2028. In short, the next two years will determine whether Rivian will succeed or fail in its high-stakes quest to become a full-stack autonomy player.
“We believe autonomy is a primary product differentiator, market share driver, and long-term value creator,” Derek Mulvey, VP for finance, said during the call.
Success is not guaranteed. Tesla has a huge head start with its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) in over 1.7 million active customer cars. articles.title: Hinter Pluto entdeckt: Algorithmus findet neuen Zwergplaneten
articles.summary:
Hinter Pluto entdeckt: Algorithmus findet neuen Zwergplaneten
Im Juni 2025 lieferte das Vera-C.-Rubin-Observatorium in Chile erste Aufnahmen des Weltalls. In den kommenden zehn Jahren soll das riesige Spiegelteleskop den südlichen Himmel systematisch erfassen und dabei erdnahe Asteroiden, Zwergplaneten oder andere Himmelsobjekte sowie -ereignisse wie Supernovae kartieren. Außerdem erhoffen sich die Astronom:innen Hinweise auf Dunkle Energie und Dunkle Materie.
2026 ED138 kreist jenseits von Pluto
Jetzt haben der Astrophysiker Matthew Holman vom Harvard & Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics und der Astronom Mario Jurić von der University of Washington einen vielversprechenden Zwergplaneten-Kandidaten aufgespürt. Der jenseits von Pluto kreisende eisige Himmelskörper firmiert derzeit unter dem Namen 2026 ED138.
Wie es in einer entsprechenden Mitteilung heißt, handelt es sich bei 2026 ED138 um einen der größten Zwergplaneten-Kandidaten im transneptunischen Bereich. Er soll einen Durchmesser von 600 bis 1.500 Kilometern haben. Zur Einordnung: Pluto ist knapp 2.400 Kilometer groß. Sollte 2026 ED138 als Zwergplanet bestätigt werden, wäre er neben Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea und Makemake erst der sechste seiner Art.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.summary:
Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection. Your origin stays private, while web application firewall (WAF), caching, bot management, and Workers work just as they do for public origins.
In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet. Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.
Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
What is generally available today
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.
Point a proxied A or AAAA record at a private IP, and Cloudflare’s application services work as they do for public origins:

While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. articles.title: Too much code, too little shipped: Why AI needs a software factory
articles.summary:
Too much code, too little shipped: Why AI needs a software factory
Can AI run the entire software show? At TechSparks 2026, ForgeCode CEO Tushar Mathur explained how AI agents can automate software development while engineers focus on quality and results.
AI can generate code faster than ever, but getting it tested and reviewed and into production is a different challenge.
Engineering teams are increasingly using AI agents to write code, fix bugs, and build features. But faster coding does not necessarily mean faster software delivery.
As code generation accelerates, reviews pile up, testing slows down, and teams struggle to coordinate the growing volume of changes.
At TechSparks 2026, Tushar Mathur, CEO of Forge Code, explored this problem in his session, Anatomy of a software factory. He explained how AI-native engineering organisations can move beyond automating individual coding tasks to building systems that manage the entire software development lifecycle.
“Just because code is becoming easy and faster to generate doesn't mean your overall SDLC becomes faster,” Mathur said.
From coding assistants to software factories
The traditional software development process focused heavily on writing code efficiently. Teams spent time defining requirements, preparing specifications and designing architecture to reduce the effort needed during implementation, he said.
With AI taking over more coding work, the bottlenecks are moving elsewhere.

articles.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
articles.summary:
4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.
The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure. Now, we are sharing a more in-depth follow up on the evidence we’ve seen of exploitation, and the progress seen on visitors patching their systems.
Let's start with the scale of the problem. A certificate authority (CA) with weak keys this serious is unprecedented, and the potential consequences are significant. While there have been plenty of compromised certification authorities in the past (such as DigiNotar, TÜRKTRUST, and TrustWave), access to their keys has always been contained to a degree; these incidents gave a limited set of attackers or organizations the ability to issue fraudulent certificates. The eMudhra incident is fundamentally different; the affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly by anyone from the public certificates themselves. articles.title: When Electric Cars Were the Clean, Quiet Choice for Women
articles.summary:
At the turn of the last century, the automobile industry was still new and evolving rapidly. In 1898, there were about 50 carmakers in the United States. A decade later, that number had increased fivefold. In 1901, the companies produced 7,000 vehicles. By 1910, production had reached 181,000.
For several decades, electric cars vied with those powered by steam and internal combustion, and nobody was sure which technology would come out on top. Steam had the legacy of locomotive technology behind it but came with a risk of fire. Steam-powered vehicles could also become exceedingly hot, depending on the placement of the boiler and the steam piping. Both gasoline and electric cars faced logistical challenges: How far could you travel without refueling or charging? You could always throw an extra can of gasoline in the back of the car, but charging a battery involved more planning. The infrastructure for long-distance travel was not yet in place.
Before the invention of the electric starter in 1911, gasoline-powered engines had to be started with a hand crank; once running, they were loud and emitted noxious fumes. Fully electric vehicles, by contrast, were easy to start; you just turned on the main battery switch, often with a key, and there was no foul exhaust to deal with.

articles.title: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren den Strombedarf von KI-Rechenzentren stemmen könnten
articles.summary:
Stromnetz am Limit: Wie Solid-State-Transformatoren jetzt Abhilfe schaffen könnten
Transformatoren sind ein zentraler, aber fast unsichtbarer Bestandteil unseres Stromnetzes: Die Großgeräte tragen dazu bei, Strom effizient über lange Entfernungen zu transportieren. Die Technik ist komplex und schwer zu bauen – immer noch. Da sich ihr grundlegendes Design seit etwa einem Jahrhundert kaum verändert hat, wären sie eigentlich reif für eine Modernisierung, doch die schien lange nicht zu passieren. Das ändert sich jetzt: Während die Welt darum kämpft, den steigenden Strombedarf von Elektrofahrzeugen, Rechenzentren und anderen Bereichen zu decken, suchen Forscher und Unternehmen nach Möglichkeiten, Transformatoren umzukrempeln. Und es gibt erste Erfolge: Neue Halbleiter-gestützte Varianten der Technik könnten dazu beitragen, Versorgungsengpässe teilweise zu lindern und sicherzustellen, dass das Stromnetz dem wachsenden Nachfragedruck standhalten kann.

articles.title: TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
articles.summary:
A high-severity vulnerability in the popular remote-access tool TeamViewer could be exploited to take over a viewer’s (an IT support technician’s) system, cybersecurity firm Remedio warns.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS score of 8.8), the flaw is described as an integer overflow affecting the remote-control screen processing component of TeamViewer clients across Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
Successful exploitation of the security defect could allow attackers to crash the viewer’s TeamViewer or execute arbitrary code on their system.
“Exploitation requires a user to establish a remote-control session to an attacker-controlled or compromised host,” TeamViewer notes in its advisory.
The issue, Remedio says, is rooted in how the host’s screen dimension is transmitted and used in the viewer: the host announces the geometry of the screen and the viewer uses the received dimensions to allocate an in-memory pixel buffer it then uses to decompress incoming screen updates.
This decode surface is only used if a hardware video decoder is not available for the session, but the host may refuse to negotiate the video codecs, thus forcing the viewer to that path.
A host can request a surface larger than what a screen can reach, and the path accepts it. An example would be 32768 by 32768 pixels at 32 bits per pixel, which overflows 32 bits, with every row past 31 being written out of bounds.

articles.title: En 1965, París empezó a excavar un aparcamiento frente a Notre-Dame. Se encontró con una ciudad romana entera bajo sus pies
articles.summary:
Hace más de 60 años, la ciudad de París ideó un plan para excavar un aparcamiento junto a su catedral más famosa. La excavación se alargó más de lo previsto, ya que sacó a la luz unos dos mil años de historia de la ciudad, apilados capa sobre capa. De hecho los restos siguen ahí, bajo el pavimento, y millones de visitantes cruzan la plaza frente a Notre-Dame cada año sin saber qué hay debajo.
Lo que hay es la Cripta Arqueológica de la Île de la Cité, un museo construido en torno a los restos que afloraron cuando París se preparaba para construir el aparcamiento a principios de la década de los 60.
Qué pasó. La excavación comenzó en 1965, justo antes de la construcción del aparcamiento subterráneo bajo la plaza, según el Ministerio de Cultura francés. Y duró hasta principios de los 70.
En los trabajos se encontraron una barbaridad de estructuras y elementos que datan de la época romana. El propio ministerio enumera un sistema de muelles galorromanos, casas con hipocaustos (calefacción bajo el suelo) y una sección de muralla de la época romana tardía.
París Musées cuenta además que se encontraron baños públicos y por encima de esas capas se encuentran niveles medievales con pozos, sótanos de casas y hasta los cimientos del Hospice des Enfants-Trouvés del siglo XVIII (la institución central donde acogían a recién nacidos y niños abandonados en la Francia del Antiguo Régimen). articles.title: Float’s Rob Khazzam on how Canadian companies should rethink AI spending | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Rob Khazzam has a funny story about keeping business AI costs under control. A few months ago, he discovered his own usage was costing $2,364 a day. He’d selected an expensive model without realizing it would remain the default for new conversations, so even routine prompts were running up the bill.
For the co-founder and CEO of Float, the Toronto-based startup building Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, it was a lesson in a challenge facing many of its nearly 10,000 customers.
“We’re seeing an explosion of spending, an explosion of adoption.”
Rob Khazzam
Float CEO

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Why Trust Is Becoming Essential for Agentic Commerce | BetaKit
articles.summary:
When tickets for your favourite artist go on sale in the middle of a critical meeting, the idea of dispatching an AI agent to buy them for you sounds pretty appealing. But how do you know it will buy the right tickets, stick to your budget, and keep your payment information safe?
“Trust is foundational to agentic commerce being able to truly scale.”
Answers to those questions are becoming more important as agentic commerce scales in Canada and AI agents move from recommending purchases to making them. A Mastercard report predicts that by 2030, more than one in 10 online shoppers will routinely use agents to shop and pay.
Making those purchases secure takes a lot of work behind the scenes, and trust built into every side of the transaction. As the buyer, you need to trust the agent to follow your instructions. The seller has to know it’s legitimately acting on your behalf, while the financial institution needs to verify that the purchase matches what you authorized before approving the payment. All of this must happen in real time, with safeguards against fraud and attempts to manipulate the agent.
Canada is already putting the technology to the test. This fall, Mastercard worked with AI company Flybits and credit card issuer Rogers Bank to complete its first Canadian transaction through Agent Pay, its agentic commerce service. articles.title: $2 Million+ Drained From Polymarket Traders in New Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
Polymarket halted trading on its international platform on October 29 after users reported unauthorized withdrawals.
According to the prediction market’s status page, the exchange was first switched to cancel-only mode, with relayer actions suspended.
“We’ve identified & fixed an issue impacting our international platform, Polymarket.com. One of our 3rd party providers was compromised, and we have referred this to relevant law enforcement. Anyone who has been impacted will be made whole,” the company said.
Trading resumed about an hour later, and Polymarket pledged to reimburse all affected traders. It has not named the vendor or disclosed losses.
Researchers have linked the theft to malicious code served from DebugBear, a UK-based website performance monitoring firm. Polymarket’s US platform was reportedly unaffected.
DebugBear confirmed being “impacted by an ongoing security incident” and urged users of its real user monitoring (RUM) product to pull its snippet from their websites. It also said it brought in specialist incident responders.
Hudson Rock obtained a copy of the malicious JavaScript from a DebugBear address used by Polymarket. The code hunted for a logged-in user’s trading tools and portfolio. Depending on the account type, it then tried either to sell positions and move the proceeds, or to send position tokens straight to an attacker-set address.

articles.title: Del cobre a la luz: cómo la fotónica podría reducir el consumo energético de la inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
La expansión de la inteligencia artificial aumenta la capacidad de cálculo requerida por los centros de datos y, con ella, la demanda de electricidad, agua y cobre. Ante ese panorama, empresas tecnológicas y laboratorios desarrollan sistemas que usan luz para transmitir información y reducir el calor de los equipos, una alternativa que podría disminuir la energía destinada a enfriarlos.
La tecnología se llama fotónica. En lugar de mover la información mediante señales eléctricas a través de cables de cobre, la transporta con luz por fibra óptica. La fibra ya se utiliza en las comunicaciones de larga distancia, pero ahora la industria busca incorporarla a las conexiones internas de estas instalaciones, entre servidores, procesadores y equipos de red.
“Creo que estamos llegando al final de la era del cobre”, afirmó Chris Sharp, director de Tecnología de Digital Realty, en declaraciones recogidas por la BBC. Con esa frase no sugirió que el metal dejará de utilizarse, sino que su peso en las conexiones internas podría disminuir.
Una instalación de 100 megavatios puede requerir unas 400 toneladas de cobre, según el medio británico. La mayor parte se destina a la red eléctrica y a los equipos de refrigeración; del total, unas 70 toneladas se usan en los servidores y cerca de 20, en el cableado que los conecta.
La transmisión de datos con luz genera menos calor
El cobre conduce las señales eléctricas con eficacia, aunque ese proceso produce calor. El efecto cobra importancia en edif…

articles.title: Binance links $6.3 billion crypto theft to compromised DevOps laptop
articles.summary:
Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has linked the theft of about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency to a DevOps engineer's compromised laptop.
The crypto exchange said the access let attackers submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions after they accessed a service container, and it hasn't yet found evidence of a leaked wallet private key.
"To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual," Binance Co-CEO Richard Teng said.
Binance also said it "uncovered additional points of breach" but was "still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them."
The company confirmed the breach in a statement shared with BleepingComputer on Thursday and reassured customers that their funds were safe.
"Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company's funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete," it said.
Since the attack, Binance has suspended deposits and withdrawals while it conducts security checks, revoked authorizations for the affected address, and is working with blockchain intelligence partners and law enforcement to trace and recover the stolen funds.

articles.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Drupal warned admins to patch a critical access bypass vulnerability in the Commerce Core module that attackers are exploiting in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118539, this flaw stems from a missing authorization weakness that can be abused by unauthenticated attackers and affects Commerce Core versions 0.0.0 through 2.41 and 3.0.0 through 3.3.13.
The Drupal security team asked admins on the 3.x branch to upgrade immediately to Commerce Core 3.3.13 (or Commerce Core 8.x-2.41 for earlier versions) and audit orders for inconsistencies, since threat actors are exploiting this vulnerability in attacks.
"This module enables you to sell goods and services to customers through an included shopping cart and checkout form or through decoupled applications via APIs," Drupal said in a Wednesday advisory tagged as highly critical.
"The module doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor. This vulnerability is being actively exploited in the wild."
Commerce Core is a community-developed Drupal module used by more than 42,000 websites, including many high-profile organizations such as Fortune 500 companies and research universities.
The module provides a software framework for building and running e-commerce sites and shopping apps on top of the Drupal Content Management System (CMS).

articles.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
articles.summary:
Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:
Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
The Project Suncatcher satellite generated a haiku about being in space.
Blue marble below
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month.
“Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.”

In 2015, biomedical entrepreneur Elizabeth Holmes was Silicon Valley’s golden girl, lauded as the youngest and richest self-made female billionaire thanks to the company she founded, Theranos, which was valued at $9 billion at the height of its success. Holmes is back in the headlines thanks to a new film, You Can See Everything, which depicts the final days before Holmes, having exhausted her appeals, went to prison. Co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, it’s a surreal, absurdist piece that has largely been received with gushing enthusiasm and no small amount of hype, with some declaring it the best film of the year. Pardon me for joining the buzzkills, but I cannot in good conscience jump on the You Can See Everything bandwagon. articles.title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
AI infrastructure company Runware is making news again, just months after unveiling the Sonic Inference Pod, a modular data center built in a factory and shipped to customers ready to install. Now the company has bigger plans. It told TechCrunch it wants to build a factory that assembles these pods on a production line, as if they were cars.
The idea isn’t entirely new. Companies like Crusoe and Schneider Electric also sell prefabricated pods, but Runware says it can ship its pods faster.
Flaviu Radulescu, co-founder and CEO of Runware, told TechCrunch that the company plans to scale production at its Romania-based factory to 30 megawatts of data center capacity per day by 2028, or nearly 1 gigawatt per month. That’s a whole lot of capacity: At that pace, Runware would produce roughly as much in a year as the entire U.S. was expected to add in data center power this year, about 10 gigawatts. But it also reflects an industrywide push to deploy data centers faster and more efficiently.
Nvidia announced, for example, the Vera Rubin AI factories and the DSX POD earlier this year. Both are also meant to make it faster and easier for companies to build their own AI data centers. The difference with Runware, though, is that it says it has actually built a factory rather than just designed the infrastructure that would let others build one.

articles.title: Run AI Models for Edge Application Development with Just a Few Commands | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI is expanding beyond the data center as developers build a new generation of agents to act at the edge: monitoring driver attention and cabin conditions, helping robots understand their surroundings and plan tasks, and coordinating fleets of machines on production lines. These physical AI applications rely on models that perceive, reason, and act within tight memory, power, and latency budgets. But getting a model ready to run can involve substantial setup.
NVIDIA DGX Spark, now available in a 64GB configuration, gives embedded developers a platform to prototype, fine-tune, and test models and agents. “Our goal is to make AI cheaper for Africa and America,” he said. “The future of AI really goes through inference.”
His argument shifts attention from the race to build more powerful models to the economics of putting them to work. For businesses using AI to answer customer enquiries or support employees, the expense recurs each time the system performs a task. Nissan has a new version of its bestselling Rogue SUV, and it’s launching the model here with the latest version of its e-Power hybrid system, which Ars tested in February. Most hybrid cars you can buy today are parallel hybrids, which means that they have an internal combustion engine and an electric motor, both of which drive some or all of the wheels—everything works in parallel. But there’s another approach. Instead of connecting the engine to the wheels via a transmission, it can act as a generator and charge the traction battery, which in turn powers the electric motor. Since the engine and motor work in series, this is known as a series hybrid.
That’s mostly how the Chevrolet Volt worked. As does Honda’s hybrid CR-V. Well, mostly; engineers worked out it was more efficient for those cars’ gasoline engines to directly drive the wheels at highway speeds, something that to this day makes a certain subset of hybrid car enthusiasts irrationally angry. If you know anyone like that in your life, send them to wherever the nearest Nissan dealership is, because the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is exactly what they’ve been asking for.

Attackers have started exploiting a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability patched earlier this month, according to the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
Tracked as CVE-2026-97229, this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the 'joaxcar' handle in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in pipeline configuration files.
CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness and could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances via a maliciously crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient expression validation.
"GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," it said.

articles.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a new high-severity WordPress vulnerability within hours of patches rolling out, Defiant warns.
Patched on October 28 in WordPress 7.1.4, the security defect impacts the WordPress update process and can be exploited for remote code execution.
According to Defiant, it is a race condition in WordPress’s Core update process that can be exploited without authentication. The attack complexity, however, is high. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the vulnerability yet.
The weakness stems from predictable, web-accessible staging paths during the upgrades. New files are unpacked into a predictable directory that is accessible from the web on many servers.
“The attacker needs a full-package update containing the installer files, public web and PHP access to the staging tree, a predictable or discovered staging path, and enough time to complete the attack before WordPress cleans up the temporary files,” Defiant explains.
According to the web security firm, threat actors are already attempting to exploit the vulnerability, polling the vulnerable paths repeatedly in their attempts to hit the seconds-long exploitability window.
While an attacker does not need an account on the site to exploit the flaw, they do need “to hit a very narrow window while WordPress is unpacking a complete Core update,” Defiant says.

Une analyse datée de juillet 2026 évalue même le risque d’une chute vers la Terre à une chance sur dix en septembre 2032 et une sur deux avant décembre 2033.
Perdre Hubble ne serait pas seulement la mort d’un symbole de l’aventure spatiale, ce serait aussi une terrible perte pour la communauté scientifique. L’engin reçoit en effet sept fois plus de demandes d’observation qu’il ne peut en traiter, malgré son ancienneté notable. Le télescope a été lancé en 1990, soit plus de 35 ans.
C’est dans ce contexte que la question d’une mission d’assistance s’est de nouveau posée dernièrement. Le centre Goddard de la Nasa, qui s’occupe de l’observatoire, a publié une demande d’informations, c’est-à-dire un appel à idées, sans engagement. articles.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
articles.summary:
SS7 and Diameter signaling attacks can track, intercept, and impersonate you. Here’s how they work and how to stop them.
Your phone can be tracked, your SMS two-factor codes can be intercepted, and your number can be impersonated, all without malware, a phishing link, or any access to your device.
The attacks happen inside the telecom network, in the carrier-to-carrier control protocols known as signaling, the automated descendants of the old telephone switchboard. Most users never see them, and most carriers can’t reliably stop them.
Signaling attacks aren’t new. Most recently, they made headlines when Iranian-linked actors reportedly exploited outdated network technology to locate the phones of US personnel in the Middle East during the Iran war.
But the vulnerability has been around for decades, and it’s been used for far more everyday crimes, like intercepting bank one-time passcodes. It has even been demonstrated by popular YouTubers: Veritasium hijacked a tech influencer’s calls and texts using only his phone number.
This keeps happening
- Criminals have reportedly exploited signaling protocols in attacks on bank accounts and global telecom infrastructure.
- Citizen Lab exposed two long-running commercial surveillance campaigns abusing SS7 and Diameter, with thousands of attacks against targets in dozens of countries.

What five P99 CONF talks reveal about database trade-offs
P99 CONF is a virtual conference on high-performance, low-latency applications. Its 2026 event ran October 21–22. Here, we cover five of its 60-plus sessions. The recordings are available on demand at p99conf.io after registration.
Database storage design balances read amplification, write amplification, and space amplification (RUM conjecture). Improving one can increase another, depending on the workload and configuration. The five talks below show how engineers make those trade-offs across different database systems.
“Can Everything be an LSM?”
Almog Gavra, Co-Founder at Responsive (now Databricks)
Gavra frames database design around read amplification (data read per result), write amplification (data written per logical write), and space amplification (storage used relative to live data). A log favors fast writes but makes reads work harder; a sorted array does the reverse. As Gavra put it, “I think about LSM trees as a mechanism for tuning between these two extremes.”
LSMs were built for local disks, but their immutable files also fit object storage. Gavra points to Amazon S3’s lower storage cost, durability, and availability, then names the trade-offs: objects must be replaced rather than edited, each GET and PUT has a price, and cold reads are slower. Smaller components and denser boards are creating new thermal challenges for ball grid array (BGA) rework. Miniature passives can be located within a millimeter or two of rework targets. This tightens thermal profile windows and raises the stakes for precision heat delivery. Traditional hot-air systems that operated at larger scales struggle to meet the demands of today’s high-density assemblies.
The SMT miniaturization trend behind modern PCB design
The drive toward higher functionality in smaller form factors has pushed surface mount technology (SMT) miniaturization to the forefront of PCB design priorities. Designers are packing more components into less space, with passive components such as 0201 and 01005 footprints increasingly used in high-density applications.
The International Electronics Manufacturing Initiative (iNEMI) electronics roadmap identifies component miniaturization and increased packing density as important industry drivers, with HDI microvia sizes continuing to shrink as manufacturers push toward finer geometries. This trend creates new challenges for rework operations that were engineered around larger geometries.
Proximity and warpage risks in high-density assemblies
As spacing tightens, the gap between a target BGA and its neighboring 0201 or 01005 passives can fall below a millimeter. Standard hot-air nozzles weren’t designed for this proximity.

Cost management for generative AI is a shared responsibility between the teams that build applications and the teams accountable for cloud spend. Many teams start by comparing per-model token rates and asking application teams to shorten prompts. Those steps help, but they don’t answer the questions that finance and engineering leaders ask as usage scales: which team spent this, on which workload, and was that spend inside an approved budget?
Agentic workloads make those questions more pressing. A conversational assistant typically issues one model invocation per user turn. An agentic workflow, such as an AI coding assistant that plans a change, reads files, calls tools, and iterates, issues many invocations per task and carries a larger context on each one. Token consumption therefore scales with the degree of autonomy you grant the workflow and the size of the context it carries, rather than with the number of user interactions. Because consumption is a function of how a workload is designed and operated, cost management for generative AI is an architectural and operational discipline. The open-source MPC Sample Key won’t be focused on chopping up drum breaks.
While the Sample Key shares many of the same controls as the MPC Sample — including the three context-sensitive encoders, a large main encoder — it seems designed for pitched sample playback, rather than chopping up drums. In fact, the “chop” button from the MPC Sample is missing entirely from the Sample Key.
The dedicated pitch and mod wheels are another clue there. While using an arpeggiator to play back drum samples can be a fun way to create rhythms, it’s more commonly used for melodic and bass parts. And a chord mode would be basically useless for drums. articles.title: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
articles.summary:
General Motors marketed its Smart Driver system as a way for parents to monitor teen drivers or for adults to track their driving behavior. But in 2024, it emerged that GM had been sharing that data with brokers. Those brokers then sold the data to insurance companies, and some drivers found that their insurance became more expensive as a result. To make matters worse, many of those drivers claimed they had no knowledge of ever agreeing to share such data for such purposes.
Last year, GM and its OnStar subsidiary entered into a settlement with the FTC, prohibiting them from sharing some kinds of driver data with third parties. The settlement was finalized this January. That agreement banned the two companies from sharing geolocation data or driver behavior data for five years. At the time, GM also discontinued Smart Driver across its entire range.
Now the automaker has reached terms with the District of Columbia and 35 states after their attorneys general joined together to sue GM as well.
GM said in a statement that “[s]afer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to being clear about what information is used, how it’s protected, and the choices customers have about what they share.”
According to TechCrunch, the settlement with the states is notable in a third party is required to assess GM’s compliance with the new privacy program.

In posts on cybercrime forums, Virtualine promoted support for various types of cybercriminal activity, including phishing, spam, carding, and more; advertised its ability to move customer services to unaffiliated infrastructure; and claimed it intentionally ignored abuse.
It also allowed users to post and sell explicit images and videos of minors and adults, and supported at least one customer that offered a hack-for-hire service aimed at stealing sexually explicit content from online accounts.
Despite receiving numerous takedown requests from law enforcement agencies in several countries, Virtualine continued to aid the customer and even helped them create a new website for uploading the illicit content. The provider continues to host the new website.
According to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs, Virtualine has been used, among others, by ransomware groups and an infostealer operator.
“Virtualine received more illicit-attributed cryptocurrency than any other TRM-labeled bulletproof hosting provider, despite receiving less total value than several peers,” the company says.

Mbene said the company’s biggest task was making a complicated product appear simple to customers, allowing businesses to accept digital assets without taking on the operational demands of managing them.
Breet, founded in 2019, converts cryptocurrency into cash for individuals in Nigeria and Ghana. It also offers an application programming interface that allows businesses to accept crypto payments and receive settlement in local currency.
The proposition separates the payment method from the currency a merchant ultimately wants to hold. Customers can pay with digital assets, while businesses receive local money without having to build a crypto operation of their own.
For Mbene, the objective is to reduce the work required to complete that transaction. “We’re just obsessed with simplicity,” she said.
That approach places much of the complexity behind the scenes. Functions such as monitoring transactions, routing deposits and converting currencies need to work together without requiring merchants to manage each step themselves.
But making the process look straightforward can create a different problem: convincing customers and business partners to trust it.
“Sometimes simplicity brings suspicion, and when it’s powered by crypto, the suspicion kind of doubles,” Mbene said.

articles.summary:
Après les calculatrices, les imprimantes et même les tests de grossesse, Doom continue de s'inviter un peu partout. Cette fois, un développeur a fait fonctionner une version simplifiée du célèbre FPS sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. Sa particularité ? Le jeu n'est pas exécuté par un moteur classique, mais recréé image après image par une intelligence artificielle.
Faire tourner Doom sur à peu près n'importe quoi est devenu une tradition chez les bidouilleurs. En 2020, Foone Turing avait même réussi à le rendre jouable sur un test de grossesse numérique, après en avoir remplacé l'écran et le processeur.
Avec son projet Tinyworldformer, le développeur SheepSeb pousse l'expérience dans une autre direction. Plutôt que d'adapter le code d'un jeu à une machine peu puissante, il a entraîné une IA à reproduire son fonctionnement. Le tout sur un Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, une carte à quelques euros équipée d'une puce RP2350, de deux cœurs pouvant atteindre 150 MHz et de seulement 520 Ko de mémoire vive. Doom avait déjà été porté sur un Raspberry Pi Pico en 2022, mais cette fois, l'expérience ne repose plus sur l'exécution du jeu original.
Un Doom lite sans moteur de jeu, mais avec deux IA
Tinyworldformer repose sur deux petits réseaux neuronaux. Le premier est un world model, ou modèle de monde : entraîné à partir de parties enregistrées, il reçoit une image et une action du joueur, puis prédit l'image suivante. Il ne calcule donc pas les conséquences des actions à partir des règles original…

articles.title: El Ayuntamiento de Madrid abre concurso para privatizar por 35 años el auditorio abandonado del parque Juan Carlos I
articles.summary:
Ya hay luz verde. O ambar, más bien: el Ayuntamiento de Madrid ha abierto el concurso para entregar en concesión el auditorio del parque Juan Carlos I, el mayor al aire libre de la capital. Han propuesto una fórmula demanial, de 35 años prorrogable a otros cinco más. Es decir, aunque el recinto seguirá siendo de dominio y titularidad pública, lo explotará un operador privado. Ya se intentó en 2021 y no fue a parar a ningún lugar. Esta vez, el plazo de ofertas termina el 24 de noviembre.
Inaugurado en 1992 en un proyecto de Antonio Fernández-Alba, el último concierto de su historia fue el de Guns N’ Roses, en 2006. Desde entonces se ha ido convirtiendo en una reliquia ruinosa. Hace ahora nueve años, en noviembre de 2017, el equipo de Ahora Madrid presionó a la competencia para su rehabilitación. Pero no fue hasta junio de 2021 cuando el Ayuntamiento anunció su estudio de viabilidad y la promesa de reformarlo. Nunca se cumplió: durante 2024 y 2025 llegaron iniciativas privadas, hasta diciembre de ese mismo año, cuando la Junta de Barajas rechazó una propuesta del PSOE para rehabilitarlo y gestionarlo con Madrid Destino.
Qué piden a cambio. Ahora mismo, sobre el papel, el adjudicatario deberá programar al menos un 60% de actividad cultural, deportiva o de ocio para el público general. El 40% restante sería para eventos privados, como congresos o ferias.

articles.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
articles.summary:
Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
Emerging evidence suggests some people with eating disorders are misusing weight-loss drugs.
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders.
A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders.
What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue.
Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says.
Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others.

articles.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
articles.summary:
For decades, passwords have been one of cybersecurity’s most persistent weaknesses. Users forget them, reuse them, share them, and surrender them to convincing phishing sites. Attackers steal credentials, automate credential stuffing, and increasingly use artificial intelligence to make social engineering more effective.
What are passkeys?
Passkeys promise to eliminate much of this problem.
Built on public-key cryptography, passkeys replace shared secrets with cryptographic credentials. There is no password for an attacker to steal, intercept through phishing, or reuse against another service. Properly implemented passkeys are also phishing-resistant because authentication is bound to the legitimate service.
That represents a significant improvement over passwords and many traditional forms of multi-factor authentication (MFA). But it does not answer a more fundamental question: Just because someone successfully authenticated, should we continue to trust that identity?
Passkeys strengthen authentication. They do not eliminate identity risk.
What Passkeys Get Right
Traditional authentication frequently relies on passwords combined with one-time passcodes, SMS messages, or push notifications. While stronger than passwords alone, these methods remain vulnerable to phishing, adversary-in-the-middle attacks, MFA fatigue, SIM swapping, and social engineering.
Passkeys fundamentally change that model. Instead of presenting a reusable secret, the user’s device holds a private cryptog…

Google Suncatcher’s prototype space data center is online and communicating with the ground after launching earlier this month alongside more than 100 other spacecraft on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.
The satellite, which carries four Google Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) and generates up to 1 kW of electricity, is intended to pave the way for future networks of close-flying satellites performing large inference workloads in orbit. However, the power demands of the TPU mean it can only turn one on for about 20 minutes at a time, complicating the already tricky business of space-to-ground communications.
After a commissioning process that tested out the satellite’s subsystems over about three weeks, the spacecraft was ready to work. When engineers on the ground sent their first prompt this week, they asked the model pre-loaded onto the satellite, Google DeepMind’s Gemma 4, to write a haiku about being in space. And thus:
Blue marble below
Data streams in silent grace
Starlight feeds my core. ✨
Google said it tested the model with these space-themed limericks (they should have sent a poet?) and, perhaps more importantly, the company asked the spacecraft to report on the orbital conditions around the satellite.
A spokesperson told TechCrunch that the satellite was operating nominally.

The new feature gives IPVanish users a static IP address that belongs to them alone

- It gives you a fixed VPN IP address that no other user shares, with five locations at launch.

IPVanish has launched a dedicated IP, an optional add-on that fills one of the most noticeable gaps in its feature list.
Until now, the provider only offered shared, dynamic IP addresses. Reviewers have repeatedly pointed to the missing option as a weak spot, particularly for remote workers and small businesses, and as recently as last week, rivals were still listing it as something IPVanish couldn't do.
NordVPN and Surfshark have offered dedicated IPs for years, so the launch brings IPVanish closer in line with the best VPN services on the market.

When you connect to a VPN normally, you share an IP address with everyone else on that server, and you might get a different one each session. A dedicated IP flips that: it's a unique address assigned to a single user, and it stays the same every time you connect.

articles.title: Analysts find looming launch crisis is "more severe" than anticipated
articles.summary:
A new report from the analytics firm Quilty Space confirms that, outside of China, the world faces a significant shortage of rockets over the next five years.
The firm estimates that between now and 2030, there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches compared to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled.
“What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved,” said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. “What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s.”
The report tallies a number of familiar factors that have gone into this crisis: the war in Ukraine taking Russian rockets off the Western market; Amazon Leo demand; developmental delays in a new generation of rockets, from New Glenn and Vulcan to Neutron, Terran R, and Nova; and more recently, the retirement of the Falcon 9 as a rocket for commercial service.
At a time when the supply of commercial rockets is contracting, demand for satellite launch is soaring, from megaconstellation operators such as Amazon to a flurry of small satellite startups. The report estimates the crunch will become most acute in 2028 but should then slowly i…

“Esto significa que los fondos indexados que invierten los ahorros de jubilación de los estadounidenses se verán obligados a comprar acciones de Anthropic aunque la acción sea volátil o esté sobrevalorada”, escribió Warren.

articles.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
articles.summary:
Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, also affects ordinary TCP connections, although remote code execution has not been publicly demonstrated on servers without an MPTCP listener.
Multipath TCP (MPTCP) is a TCP feature that lets a single connection use multiple network paths at the same time to improve performance and reliability. It is commonly used in environments where devices have multiple network connections, such as Wi-Fi and cellular networks.
CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free vulnerability in the kernel's IPv4 TCP networking code that received a severity score of 9.8 out of 10 from the Linux kernel CVE team.
The vulnerability affects Linux kernels dating back to version 4.4, including widely used distributions such as Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and Rocky Linux.
According to the Linux kernel advisory, the vulnerability stems from a race condition in how the kernel handles TCP connection requests, potentially causing a use-after-free condition.
"tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it," reads the advisory.

On July 2, 2026, the Supreme Court of India quashed orders passed by the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal in the Pooja Ramesh Singh v. One Civic owner purchased a cheap aftermarket head unit off Amazon, and decided to have Claude work its magic on it, like it would a smart TV. What was reportedly discovered isn’t surprising, but is worth knowing about.

articles.title: From Beginner to Bug Hunter: Learning Cybersecurity in the AI Era.
articles.summary:
Finding a real security flaw and getting paid for it is an appealing goal when you are learning cyber security. Bug bounties give you a chance to test your skills on real software and help its developers make it safer.
Headlines about programs closing or pausing under a flood of AI reports can make that route feel less certain.
Earlier this year, curl, the widely used data transfer tool and library, ended its paid bounty program after similar problems.
As a beginner, these decisions raise a practical question about where to put your effort.
A useful starting point is understanding what went wrong, then building the skills to produce findings that someone else can verify.
Why some bug bounty programs are pulling back
A bug bounty program rewards eligible security findings under a defined set of rules. Developers must still review each submission, reproduce the issue and assess its impact.
A convincing report about an imaginary vulnerability can consume time that a small security team needs for genuine problems.
When curl ended its program on January 31, 2026, maintainer Daniel Stenberg explained how the quality of submissions had deteriorated. He confirmed vulnerabilities fell from above 15% in previous years to below 5% starting in 2025. Across its lifetime, the program had helped uncover 87 confirmed vulnerabilities and paid researchers more than $100,000.
Those figures describe curl’s experience specifically.

articles.title: Un agujero negro que se parte en dos suena imposible. Un nuevo estudio dice que la física deja una rendija abierta
articles.summary:
La física de los agujeros negros está rodeada aún de muchas preguntas sin resolver. Por ejemplo, sabemos que dos agujeros negros pueden fusionarse para dar lugar a uno más grande, ¿pero puede un gran agujero negro dividirse en dos más pequeños? Tradicionalmente se ha pensado que no, pues iría en contra de las leyes de la física. Sin embargo, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad Federico II de Nápoles, la Sorbona de París y la Universidad del Sur de Dinamarca acaba de encontrar un atajo teórico por el que sí sería posible.
Una cuestión de orden. Según la segunda ley de la termodinámica, la entropía de un sistema aislado siempre tiende a aumentar. A muy grandes rasgos, la entropía hace referencia al desorden, o la cantidad de conformaciones microscópicas distintas que puede alcanzar dicho sistema. Por eso, siempre se dice que el Universo tiende al desorden.
Generalmente, en la mayoría de objetos, la entropía es proporcional a la cantidad de materia, por lo que si se rompe en dos un pedazo de papel su entropía no disminuirá, ya que la suma de los dos pedazos sigue siendo la misma. Con los agujeros negros, la cosa cambia, ya que en ellos la entropía es proporcional al área del horizonte de sucesos, que crece con el cuadrado de la masa irreducible del agujero negro. Si un agujero negro se divide en dos, el área de sus horizontes de sucesos será más pequeña, de modo que la entropía disminuye. Iría contra las leyes de la física.

articles.title: How Ghana’s TrustCheck helps shoppers vet online sellers before they pay - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Ghanaian startup TrustCheck has built a review and trust platform that allows consumers to check out businesses, especially social media sellers, before they part with their money.
Launched in January of this year by Elliot Brenya, Tema-based TrustCheck lets users look up a business, read verified customer reviews, and see a trust score out of 100. The score combines a business’s rating, review volume, how responsive it is to customers, verification status and any open disputes.
“A lot of buying in Ghana now happens on Instagram, TikTok, X and WhatsApp. You see a product, message the seller, send money by Mobile Money and hope it arrives,” Brenya told Disrupt Africa. “Most of the time it does, but when it doesn’t, there is usually no way to get your money back and no record that warns the next person. TrustCheck is meant to be that record.”
Brenya was inspired to build the platform after being scammed while buying a mobile device, having relied on fake ratings for the vendor.
All reviews on TrustCheck are moderated before going live, and reviewers can attach proof of purchase, such as MoMo receipts or order chats, which only moderators can see. Businesses cannot pay to have reviews removed, but can claim their pages for free, respond to reviews and apply for verification. This month the startup also launched a scam check for phone numbers, MoMo numbers, social media handles and websites, as well as a public API that returns a business’s trust score.

Intel reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year over year, as expanded data center demand offset manufacturing bottlenecks and a sharp contraction in personal computer sales.
The results reflect a structural divide in the technology hardware sector. While AI infrastructure drives chip sales for server processors and memory suppliers, component shortages and elevated memory prices increase system costs and weigh on consumer hardware demand.
Data center demand collides with manufacturing bottlenecks
Intel’s Data Center and AI group generated $7.3 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 78% year over year, reflecting strong demand across hyperscale, enterprise, and cloud customers.
However, shortages of raw materials, substrates, and other critical components limited Intel’s ability to meet demand for its Xeon server family. A two-week shutdown at an Intel fabrication facility in Israel, following a gas explosion, further impacted production.
Because turning silicon wafers into finished chips takes roughly three months, wafers that were still in process when the fab shut down will likely be scrapped. Intel CFO David Zinsner said during the earnings call most of those write-offs should land in the fourth quarter, and he does not expect further scrapping in the first quarter. He said the fab disruption will have an estimated $300 million impact on revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, with a similar impact in the first quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Google: Agentic AI Will Drive New Demands on Data Center CPUs - EE Times
articles.summary:
The requirements of agentic AI are placing new demands on data center CPUs and infrastructure as a whole, Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager for AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, told EE Times.
“Chat is relatively straightforward—there’s a question and an answer, and it relies heavily on inference across GPUs or TPUs,” he said. “With agents, the nature of those interactions is changing quite a bit.”
With agents, the user’s high-level intent can be broken down into subtasks and assigned to a team of agents that can access other APIs, visit websites, write and run code—CPU tasks. Sessions can be much longer and can involve multiple human users, which means context and state need to be preserved over potentially days or weeks.
“Agents are often bursty, and often idle,” he said. “They don’t do anything for [say] a day or two until you come back to them, or maybe until some API responds… It’s unique from older CPU workloads, in that it needs to be stateful over a long period of time, but is often idle during that period of time, and then when it’s not idle, it’s highly bursty.”
Handling this in a performant and secure way is a big challenge the industry is facing today, Lohmeyer said.
“Demand is already very high and is growing rapidly,” he said. “So, how do we provide the infrastructure that can support that growth and do it cost-effectively?”

articles.title: Esta nueva memoria promete resolver uno de los mayores problemas creados por la IA
articles.summary:
La industria de los semiconductores atraviesa una de las peores crisis desde la pandemia. La explosión de la IA ha disparado la demanda de memoria a niveles nunca antes vistos, lo cual generó una escasez y aumento de precios que han golpeado a todos los segmentos, incluidos los móviles. Este escenario podría cambiar gracias a la Z2RAM, una nueva tecnología impulsada por el antiguo jefe de Intel, Pat Gelsinger.
De acuerdo con un reporte de The Register, la propuesta de la Z2RAM intenta combinar las ventajas de las tres tecnologías que dominan el mercado: SRAM, DRAM y NAND.
La SRAM es extremadamente rápida y se utiliza en las memorias caché de los procesadores, pero ocupa mucho espacio y es costosa de escalar. Mientras tanto, la DRAM ofrece una mayor densidad y es la base de la memoria RAM convencional, aunque es más lenta. Por último, la NAND, que se usa en los SSD, se distingue por su capacidad y fabricación en múltiples capas verticales.
Nagare Labs, una startup respaldada por Geslinger, intenta reunir lo mejor de estos tres mundos. Según la compañía, Z2RAM podría ofrecer la velocidad de la SRAM, la densidad de la DRAM y la arquitectura de la NAND en un mismo paquete. Esta nueva memoria sería escalable y tendría un consumo energético mucho menor, convirtiéndose en una alternativa para las empresas de IA.
¿Qué es la Z2RAM, la nueva memoria que podría acabar con el RAMaggeddon?

articles.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
articles.summary:
Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one.
A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It’s very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says.
A filtered collection
“We don’t fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth,” Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars’ gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.”
That left scientists with a biased collection.
“Even to date, none of our collected Martian meteorites are similar to what we found on the surface,” Liu said. The partial exception is Black Beauty, which has a bulk chemistry that matches orbital measurements. But…

articles.title: Binance loses $6.3 billion in largest crypto heist ever
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, has suffered a cyberattack believed to be the largest crypto theft in history. Crypto worth more than $6 billion has been stolen from the platform, which initially suspended customer deposits and withdrawals. It's believed that a North Korean hacking unit was responsible for the attack.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs puts the haul at approximately $6.36 billion, taken from Binance wallets across ten blockchains on October 29. Most of the money was moved in about 20 minutes. The firm attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit, with high confidence.
There is some good news for customers. Binance says it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets and will cover all losses. Deposits are now operating normally, although withdrawals remain suspended. The exchange said on Friday that it expected withdrawals to resume within the next day or two.
The initial investigation pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. Binance said this allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. It added that it had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked.
However, the company subsequently said investigators had uncovered additional points of breach, describing the incident as a complex attack – so the compromised laptop is unlikely to be the whole story. Binance has promised to release more…

Prosecutors say the hacking conspiracy Agha took part in was directed by figures close to Bashar al-Assad, among them the head of Syria’s General Intelligence Directorate. The scheme began as early as August 2011 and continued until January 2024.
The DOJ described Agha as a central figure in the operation. He compromised around 47 targets, a mix of Western news outlets, companies, NGOs, and government bodies in the US and allied countries.
Among the intrusions highlighted by prosecutors was the 2013 takeover of the Associated Press’s Twitter account. Agha used it to publish a fabricated report claiming that President Barack Obama had been hurt in two blasts at the White House. The fake post triggered a flash crash that briefly wiped $136 billion off the combined value of the Dow Jones Industrial Average’s component stocks.
Agha also gained access to the company hosting the Marine Corps’ recruiting website and sent its traffic to an image calling on Marines to defy their orders.

Understanding the Rising Threat of Business Email Scams
In today’s fast-paced business environment, email remains a primary communication tool, especially for financial transactions like invoicing and payments. However, this reliance has made businesses, particularly their finance teams and bookkeepers, prime targets for increasingly sophisticated email scams. One of the most prevalent tactics involves fake invoice scams, where cybercriminals impersonate legitimate vendors or partners to trick businesses into paying fraudulent invoices.
The scale of this threat is staggering. With 94% of malware delivered via email and phishing attacks accounting for over 90% of data breaches, email-based scams have become the favored method for cybercriminals aiming to exploit businesses. According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center, business email compromise (BEC) scams led to losses exceeding $2.4 billion in 2023 alone. These numbers reflect not only the monetary damage but also the operational disruptions and reputational harm businesses face.
As these scams evolve, understanding their anatomy is critical to strengthening defenses. This article delves into how fake invoices slip past busy bookkeepers, what makes these scams so effective, and crucially, how businesses can protect themselves.

articles.title: Basically no one is using AI agents for their DoorDash orders

As AI tools and agents have continued their march across all aspects of digital life, many companies are trying to use LLMs to improve the experience of purchasing goods and services on the Internet. Thus far, though, a vanishingly small number of people seem to be taking advantage of those capabilities, at least when it comes to using the popular food delivery app DoorDash with an outside AI agent.
In a third-quarter earnings call Thursday, DoorDash co-founder and CEO Tony Xu responded to an analyst question by noting that “AI agents are generating several hundred orders [on DoorDash] across the time that they’ve been up and running.” In a marked understatement, Xu called this a “very low use case” for a company that handled just shy of 1 billion orders total in the third quarter of 2026 alone.
Speaking generally, Xu said he sees the potential for AI agents to be genuinely helpful for “long consideration purchases” and major decisions where agents would be “doing work on your behalf proactively in the background.” However, Xu added, “when it comes to a task that’s as simple as ordering food, we tend to see that come directly to DoorDash.”
Give it time?
To be fair to the AI boosters, DoorDash only rolled out its Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector less than a month ago. The connector provides a standardized, open-standard way for third-party AI tools to easily order through DoorDash’s platform. articles.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
articles.summary:
A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don’t need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time.
In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both.
But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn’t be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That’s despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat.
Further, while the data suggests many patients were being dishonest, clinicians responded with what could be considered their own form of dishonesty; in most cases, the dubious fibs led to antibiotic prescriptions. articles.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
articles.summary:
Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path. First adopters include stateful, high-throughput streaming workloads. Here, a neighbor's interference can lead to minutes of checkpoint recovery.
Titus launches millions of containers a week across tens of thousands of EC2 instances and is multi-tenant by default. Netflix says that cgroups, seccomp, the iocost controller, and traffic shaping can’t split shared hardware. This includes resources like the last-level cache and memory bandwidth. Its HTB traffic shaper also takes a global lock. A container that floods the host with small packets can burn the kernel CPU and starve its neighbors. Predictive CPU pinning and eBPF-based detection helped, but Netflix concluded that shared-kernel tuning narrows the gap without closing it.
Netflix rejected the alternatives for specific reasons. MicroVMs such as Firecracker and Kata need bare-metal or nested virtualization, and nested virtualization was not ready on Netflix's instance types. They also meant running a hypervisor layer, added virtualization overhead, and lacked GPU support. gVisor added overhead on I/O-heavy paths, and a single vendor does most of its maintenance. Josep Albors, responsable de Investigación y Concienciación de ESET España, comenta: “Para la mayoría de los usuarios, que nos enfrentamos a amenazas más mundanas, este consejo, en materia de ciberseguridad, sirve de poco”. Además, dependiendo de cómo se instale y active, el programa malicioso tendrá efecto o no.
“Solo se aplica para casos concretos en los que el malware está presente en la memoria RAM, que se borra cuando reinicias el dispositivo”, explica Albors. El problema de esta memoria es que es temporal y se vacía al apagar el teléfono. En el caso de que la infección solo se active en memoria (sin persistencia), puede ser interrumpida por el apagado.
El problema es que, si el software malicioso está instalado en el terminal, al apagar y encender el móvil no va a desinstalar la app maligna. Así pues, puede volver a activarse al encenderlo. Además, no podemos estar seguros de que la infección haya desaparecido por el hecho de que el móvil vuelva a funcionar correctamente. Es necesario conocer la naturaleza de la amenaza y trabajar sobre su causa.

Una diferencia que se debe a una divergencia fundamental en sus prioridades, expectativas y formación. Los críticos profesionales evalúan una película bajo una lente analítica, prestando atención a la estructura técnica, la innovación del guion y la coherencia temática. Algo que a menudo los lleva a celebrar propuestas experimentales, de autor o que desafían los tropos tradicionales.
Por el contrario, la gran mayoría de la audiencia general acude al cine buscando entretenimiento, evasión emocional o una conexión directa con los personajes. Esta disparidad hace que los espectadores premien con entusiasmo películas comerciales de fórmula que ofrecen diversión inmediata, mientras que los críticos las califican de predecibles o perezosas. Investors are getting nervous about AI infrastructure spending just as the Big Tech companies double down.

But as we enter the fourth quarter, that enthusiasm seems to be giving way to concerns about negative free cash flow (spending more cash than a company brings in), mounting debt, and whether these enormous investments will ever generate enough returns.
The anxiety spilled across the market on Friday. The Nasdaq fell 2.9%, and chip stocks took a drubbing, too: Nvidia dropped 4%, Broadcom more than 5%, and Qualcomm 11%. Alphabet, which plummeted 12% on Thursday, its worst day on record, wiping out $500 billion in market value, fell again.

Alphabet provided the clearest example of that this week. Mais ce nouveau système de fonctionnement que Reddit souhaite mettre en place vise surtout à protéger la plate-forme contre le scraping (l’extraction) non autorisé de ses données par les intelligences artificielles. Hubble va retomber sur Terre : la NASA appelle à l’aide pour sauver son télescope légendaire, vieux de 36 ans
Sans moteur et freiné chaque jour par la haute atmosphère, le télescope spatial le plus célèbre du monde a une chance sur deux de replonger vers la Terre d’ici fin 2033. La NASA invite les industriels à le remonter, à le réparer ou à lui offrir une fin maîtrisée. Seule ombre au tableau : la dernière tentative de ce genre a viré au fiasco cet été.

Les entreprises ont jusqu'au 30 novembre pour expliquer comment elles relèveraient son orbite, moderniseraient ses équipements ou piloteraient sa rentrée dans l'atmosphère. Le calendrier est serré. Faute de propulsion, Hubble devrait rentrer dans l'atmosphère entre 2033 et 2034, selon le communiqué de l'agence, et toute mission devra donc avoir lieu d'ici 2032.
	
Hubble a encore une science importante devant lui, et nous devrions examiner chaque occasion raisonnable de le faire travailler le plus longtemps possible.
Le patron de l'agence a de bonnes raisons d'insister. Malgré Webb et le tout nouveau télescope Roman, aucun successeur capable d'observer dans l'ultraviolet et le visible avec la même finesse n'est attendu avant les années 2040.

The same factories are busy with far pricier boards for AI servers, so PC orders are getting pushed to the back of the line.

The trouble is that a high-end AI server board can stack dozens of layers of low-loss laminate and specialty glass fabric. So each one ties up far more material and factory time than a desktop motherboard ever would. Cloud giants are happy to pay up for them – Amazon even bought a roughly NT$1.59 billion stake in Taiwanese board maker Gold Circuit Electronics in September.

articles.title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
articles.summary:
Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.
The problem is particularly acute for large AI training jobs. A model may run for weeks across hundreds of GPUs, with all workers operating in lockstep. A single failed GPU, degraded network adapter, or slow machine can therefore stop or significantly slow the entire workload. Netflix has built its GPU compute platform on Kubernetes and designed it to detect these failures, remove unhealthy capacity automatically, and allow long-running jobs to recover from machine loss.
The approach has produced measurable results: Netflix reports more than 99.95% GPU-node availability and an increase in job success from approximately 98% to more than 99.5%.
A conventional cloud health check can establish that a virtual machine is running and reachable, but that does not mean its GPUs are capable of running a distributed training workload.
Netflix found that a GPU can respond normally to a status query while failing once memory is allocated or sustained computation begins. Similarly, a network adapter may be present but have fewer links than expected, allowing collective operations to continue at severely reduced bandwidth.

articles.title: Anthropic expected to receive high 'junk' rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says | TechCrunch
