Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times.
The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around.
Now Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting.
TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.
Blackstone’s forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business. The lab has been on a spending spree, racking up large compute power deals throughout the past 12 months, which has worried investors.
Anthropic officially filed to go public earlier this week, kicking off a wave of speculation about how the massive IPO would impact the broader AI industry.

The serving path retrieves this prepared data and resolves each item against the current catalog. It first tries to match the original store item, then a catalog product identifier, and finally a search term. Starten soll die App bereits zum 2.Januar 2027. Damit setzt Deutschland Vorgaben aus der EU um. D-you ist also die deutsche Version der European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI‑Wallet). Außerdem braucht die Ausweisfunktion eine Internetverbindung. Geht das Handy verloren, muss die Wallet ohne Backup komplett neu eingerichtet werden.
Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Ab Ende 2027 sind dann auch Banken, Energieversorger, Telekommunikationsanbieter und sehr große Online-Plattformen verpflichtet, die Wallet zu nutzen. articles.title: Google Discloses PageBreak AI Security Agent That Found 500+ XSS Bugs
articles.summary:
According to a paper published by Google, its AI-powered security agent has uncovered more than 500 XSS vulnerabilities across its web applications since entering full operation in January. Google PageBreak uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities, but reports them only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application, resulting in a near-zero false-positive rate.
With PageBreak, every vulnerability hypothesis is tested against a running environment with a real exploit, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing to a world-readable location for path traversal, or triggering outbound DNS for RCE. Michał Bentkowski, information security engineer at Google, explains:
Early on in the development of PageBreak, we made a conscious decision to prioritize deterministic validation. Rather than simply hypothesizing bugs based on code patterns, the system closes the loop by verifying potential flaws against running environments. This approach results in a near-zero false positive rate, ensuring that we avoid overloading product teams with unverified vulnerability reports.
Google also retains non-deterministic findings internally to seed deeper future scans, identify gaps in its validation capabilities, and guide the development of new validators. These unverified candidates are not sent to product teams, keeping their attention focused on high-confidence vulnerabilities. Bentkowski writes:

Le champ magnétique terrestre piège des particules énergétiques dans deux grands anneaux en forme de beignet, les ceintures de Van Allen. Les chercheurs l’ont baptisée « barrière impénétrable ».
Son origine reste débattue. articles.summary:
Año 1922, la Unión Soviética levanta en Moscú una torre de acero que pretendía rivalizar con la Torre Eiffel de París. Aquella mole sobrevivió a Stalin, a la Segunda Guerra Mundial y a la desaparición del país que la había construido. Más de un siglo después, su futuro está en manos de las autoridades rusas, que consideran demasiado costoso restaurarla y plantean desmontarla para levantar una versión nueva. Sí, Rusia está dispuesta a conservar la idea de uno de sus mayores prodigios de ingeniería, incluso si para hacerlo tiene que destruirla.
La Torre Eiffel soviética. La Torre Shújov, situada al sur del centro de Moscú, fue encargada por Lenin y terminada en 1922. Diseñada por el ingeniero Vladímir Shújov, alcanza los 148 metros y está formada por una sucesión de estructuras hiperbólicas de acero entrelazado.
Su función era transmitir señales de radio por el territorio soviético y simbolizar las ambiciones tecnológicas del nuevo Estado comunista. La ligereza de su diseño la convirtió en una referencia de la arquitectura moderna y en una respuesta simbólica a la Torre Eiffel, inaugurada en París en 1889.
Un siglo resistiendo. La estructura atravesó las purgas estalinistas, la invasión alemana de la Unión Soviética y el colapso del régimen en 1991. Su deterioro llegó de una forma mucho menos espectacular, con décadas de mantenimiento insuficiente. Projetos de código aberto permitem rodar títulos exclusivos em outras plataformas, mas exigem uma cópia original dos games.
Uma semana após o primeiro jailbreak do Nintendo Switch 2 via software, diversos jogos exclusivos da Nintendo já rodam em outras plataformas. Publicações no X/Twitter mostram títulos do console funcionando em PCs, no iPhone 18 Pro e até em um computador com macOS.
Ferramentas de código aberto têm facilitado o processo, como o software ns2jb, disponibilizado em 22 de outubro. Jogos como Mario Kart World, Dragon Age e Zelda foram disponibilizados em ports no GitHub sob a licença MIT, que permite o acesso ao código para pesquisa e testes. São projetos que não incluem os jogos em si: para executá-los, é necessário ter uma cópia original de cada título.
Por isso, a disponibilização dos ports, por si só, não configura pirataria. A infração ocorre quando há distribuição ou download não autorizado das imagens ISO dos títulos.
A Nintendo, porém, tem um histórico de ações contra emuladores e ferramentas de acesso a seus jogos. Em 2024, a empresa conseguiu derrubar o Yuzu, conhecido emulador de Nintendo Switch, e pediu a remoção de outras ferramentas semelhantes hospedadas no GitHub.
Mais recentemente, um usuário do Reddit foi condenado a pagar US$ 4,5 milhões (pouco mais de R$ 24 milhões) por violações envolvendo mais de 30 jogos exclusivos do Switch.

articles.title: Intel stock plunges nearly 30%, its worst day in 52 years
articles.summary:
What just happened? Intel was one of the stock market's biggest surprises this year. Its shares nearly quadrupled between January and a record high in late June – a run fueled by demand for the CPUs behind agentic AI. But on Friday, the chipmaker gave back a huge chunk of those gains in a single session. The stock closed down almost 29% at $65.76, its worst day since 1974.
Oddly enough, the quarter itself went well. Intel beat Wall Street's earnings estimates. Its data center revenue jumped nearly 80% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, too. But its forecast for the last three months of the year landed well short: analysts had penciled in about $17 billion in revenue. Intel only expects $15 billion to $16 billion.
The weak spot is PCs. AI data centers are buying up so much of the world's memory that laptops and desktops have gotten a lot pricier this year. So fewer of them are selling. Intel now expects PC shipments to drop about 12% in 2026 and another 10% in 2027. It doesn't see things improving until memory supply and prices get back to normal.
The forecast also has to absorb a shutdown at the company's fab in Kiryat Gat, Israel. That's where an explosion killed two workers earlier this month.
Going by Yahoo Finance's count of closing prices back to 1973, only a nearly 30% slide in July 1974 was worse than Friday. Bank of America, D.A. Davidson, Seaport and Roth all downgraded the stock to neutral the same day. The US government felt it too, since its roughly 10% stake lo…

Was ist eigentlich das älteste Programm mit grafischer Oberfläche (GUI), das ohne Emulation oder Modifikation noch unter Windows 11 läuft? Dieser Frage widmete sich der Programmierer Boris Popik und kam zu einigen überraschenden Erkenntnissen.
Keine 16-Bit-Unterstützung in Windows 11
Wie Popik in seinem Blog erklärt, bietet Windows 11 keine native Unterstützung von 16-Bit-Anwendungen. Das bedeutet, dass die Suche erst in der frühen Windows-NT-Ära Anfang der 1990er-Jahre beginnen kann. Das von Microsoft entwickelte 32-Bit-Betriebssystem kam im Juli 1993 auf den Markt.
In einem Forum wurde Popik auf Win32s aufmerksam gemacht, einer Erweiterung für Windows 3.1 und Windows 3.11 und einer Art Brückentechnologie für den Übergang in das 32-Bit-Zeitalter. Mit Win32s war es möglich, bestimmte 32-Bit-Programme auf dem älteren 16-Bit-Windows zum Laufen zu bringen.
Freecell von 1993 zum Laufen gebracht

articles.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Salesforce has agreed to acquire Rune Technologies, a startup that builds AI software to help the U.S. military predict supply needs and manage logistics from the field, for $375 million in cash and stock, Resilience Media reported.
The acquisition underscores Salesforce’s push into defense tech through Missionforce, its business unit serving national security and defense agencies. Since Missionforce launched last year, its business has grown 80% year over year, driven in part by a new 10-year, $5.6 billion contract with the U.S. Army, the company said in a blog post. By integrating Rune’s frontline logistics data, Missionforce will extend beyond back-office administrative planning to support battlefield operations.
Since its founding in 2024, Rune has raised a total of $30 million from investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Point72 Ventures, and IQT, a CIA-backed nonprofit venture firm formerly known as In-Q-Tel. The startup was last valued at $127 million when it raised a Series A led by Human Capital last year, according to PitchBook.
Salesforce has been on an acquisition spree this year. In addition to Rune, the CRM giant agreed to buy AI agent platform Fin (formerly Intercom) for $3.6 billion, bought Qualified for $1.2 billion, and signed an agreement to buy Listen Labs after the startup walked away from a $125 million Series C term sheet at a $1.5 billion valuation, as TechCrunch reported.
Salesforce didn’t respond to a request for comment.

These devices offer convenience and efficiency, allowing healthcare professionals to access patient records quickly and provide timely care. However, with these benefits come significant privacy challenges. Ensuring patient data remains secure on shared tablets is critical to maintaining trust, complying with regulations, and protecting sensitive health information.
More clinics and small health practices are turning to shared tablets to improve workflow and reduce paperwork. According to a 2023 survey by the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society (HIMSS), 68% of small healthcare providers reported using mobile devices such as tablets for patient data access, up from 45% in 2019. This rapid adoption highlights the importance of understanding and managing the privacy risks associated with shared device usage.
Healthcare providers are legally obligated to protect patient data under regulations such as HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) in the United States and similar privacy laws worldwide. Compliance requires organizations to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards to secure electronic protected health information (ePHI).

articles.title: L'ancien patron d'Intel croit avoir trouvé une solution à la crise de la RAM
articles.summary:

La crise des composants mémoire et la hausse des prix continuent d'impacter durement les divers appareils informatiques grand public. Smartphones, tablettes, PC… Tout a augmenté, même les consoles ! Cette crise, pas près de se terminer, pourrait toutefois trouver une issue grâce à une nouvelle technologie baptisée Z2RAM.
Développée par Nagare Labs, une entreprise cofondée par les professeurs Suman Datta et Shimeng Yu du Georgia Institute of Technology, elle bénéficie d'un financement de 5 millions de dollars mené par Playground Global, dont Pat Gelsinger, ancien PDG d'Intel, est un associé.
Une architecture combinant trois technologies de mémoire
La Z2RAM ambitionne de réunir la rapidité de la SRAM, la densité de la DRAM et les possibilités d'empilement vertical de la NAND, avec une consommation énergétique réduite et une fabrication nettement simplifiée.
La SRAM, utilisée dans les caches des processeurs, est rapide mais occupe beaucoup de place. La DRAM, utilisée dans les si chères barrettes de RAM, offre une densité supérieure, mais une vitesse moindre. Quant à la NAND des SSD, elle privilégie la densité grâce à son empilement vertical, au détriment des performances.

articles.title: Home Battery vs Generator vs Grid: What Keeps Your Home Running in a Blackout? - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A blackout can occur at any time, without warning. There are several reasons for a blackout, such as issues with the electrical grid, severe weather, and other local problems. When the electricity goes out, home appliances stop working. To maintain your daily routine during a blackout, a backup power supply can help you run your home appliances.
To prevent a home from a blackout, there are three options: an electricity grid, a solar battery, and a backup generator. These three options work completely differently from one another.
Does Solar Power Work During a Blackout?
Yes, solar power works during a blackout, but only when you add a solar battery to your solar system. Most homeowners misunderstand that installing solar panels automatically means energy independence, but it’s true if you pair your rooftop panels with a solar battery from a trusted solar panel installer like Solar 365.
In general, when solar systems are grid-connected, the solar inverter shuts down when the grid goes offline for safety reasons. To prevent electricity from being sent back into the network while electrical workers are doing line work or repairing electrical wires in any other area.
To provide home backup, a solar system needs a suitably sized battery and backup equipment installed by a licensed solar panel installer, capable of safely disconnecting the home or property from the grid.
This is where batteries and generators can become useful.

articles.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to third state and are attacking pets
articles.summary:
For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people’s pets.
This week, the country’s New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.
The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.
Because of their ability to ravage livestock, the flies were eliminated from the country in the 1960s through aerial releases of sterile male flies, which thwart successful breeding. For years, they were held at bay using a biological barrier along the Darién Gap at the border of Panama and Colombia. But the barrier was breached in 2022, and the flies have made their way back to the US through Central America.
No one is safe
While they are largely seen as a threat to the livestock industry, they can also devastate wildlife, domestic pets, and in rarer cases, humans. articles.title: PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
articles.summary:
PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks — 8x8 lab prototype loses less light than rivals, with plans to develop larger devices
Google’s mirror switches have 136 ports; PsiQuantum’s chip has eight, with larger devices in development.
PsiQuantum, a quantum computing company, announced in a release earlier this week that it has turned its low-loss silicon photonics into an optical switch for use in AI data centers. Every optical switch typically comes with loss of light: the more light a switch receives, the less reaches the other side, with the amount of light lost measured in decibels. Typical data center optics can tolerate half the light (3 dB) being lost. PsiQuantum's switch debuted with a demo that typically loses only 1.2 dB of signal, or about a quarter of the light in lab tests, and the all-optical switch can achieve it without an amplifier. The prototype is, however, comparatively small, with eight inputs and outputs (8x8) against competitors’ 32 to 300, but the company says larger devices are in development.
The optical circuit switch (OCS) passes light straight through, from fiber to fiber, without converting it to or from electrical signals. Regular data center switches make that conversion at every hop, which takes power and adds latency. An OCS, instead, uses a fixed light path that it maintains until a change is ordered. articles.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
articles.summary:
The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century.
NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope’s orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.
The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies’ current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope’s performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.
“The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032,” NASA wrote in the RFI. The contractor would be responsible for providing the launch vehicle, servicing spacecraft, mission operations, and “crew if applicable.”
No commitments yet

Fortanix has announced support for Confidential Containers in its Confidential AI platform. The integration connects Kubernetes workload attestation to encryption-key release, so workloads that meet security policy can decrypt models and sensitive data inside hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs).
Confidential Containers (CoCo), a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project, runs Kubernetes pods inside confidential virtual machines backed by hardware-based trusted execution environments (TEEs). Unlike ordinary containers, whose isolation depends largely on the host operating system, confidential VMs use hardware protections to encrypt memory and restrict access to the workload while it runs. This helps protect data in use, not just data at rest or in transit, and can let teams run sensitive workloads on shared infrastructure. Those protections still depend on trusting the guest software and configuring attestation and key release correctly.
Fortanix's technical overview describes plugins connecting CoCo workloads to two services: Confidential Computing Manager (CCM), which verifies the environment, and Data Security Manager (DSM), which releases keys only to environments CCM has verified. articles.title: « Le SMS de la mort » : ce simple message peut rendre votre smartphone inutilisable
articles.summary:
Le chercheur indépendant en cybersécurité Mark Blaszczyk a rendu publique une faille zero day sur Android. Pas de panique, elle a été corrigée par Google avant et votre téléphone ne court aucun risque. Mais le fonctionnement de cette faille est tout à fait intéressant.
Un « SMS of Death » qui peut faire des dégâts sur votre smartphone Android
Mark Blaszczyk a donc publié le résultat de ses recherches sur Internet et il décrit en détail comment fonctionne cette faille. Elle se trouve dans le composant Android plus très utilisé, un ancien format de « data SMS », utilisé historiquement pour des notifications de MMS ou des contenus push. Il n’apparaît jamais à l’écran, puisqu’il se contente de fonctionner en arrière-plan. Le problème vient en réalité d’une conversion mal encadrée : Android lit la longueur de l’en-tête d’un message comme un entier long, puis la convertit en entier signé 32 bits sans vérifier que la valeur reste plausible.
Avec la séquence de cinq octets 88 80 80 80 00, cette valeur devient -2147483648. Face à ça, Android tente alors de créer un tableau d’octets de cette taille négative, ce qui tue le processus com.android.phone qui gère… la téléphonie, rien que ça. Chaque message malformé comme cela coupe donc le service durant une à deux secondes, le temps que ce processus redémarre. Ce qui coupe tout simplement les appels en cours.
Une faille bien particulière, puisqu’elle est qualifiée de zero click, c’est-à-dire que la victime n’a rien à ouvrir, installer ou v…

articles.title: Qué es la dirección IP, cómo encontrarla y por qué es importante para navegar por internet
articles.summary:
Cada vez que una persona ingresa a una página web, utiliza una aplicación o conecta su celular a una red Wi-Fi, su dispositivo necesita identificarse para intercambiar información. En ese proceso interviene la dirección IP, un número que permite reconocer a los equipos dentro de una red y hacer posible la comunicación a través de internet.
Aunque suele pasar desapercibida, esta identificación digital cumple una función fundamental en la navegación cotidiana. También puede resultar útil cuando una conexión presenta fallas, se necesita configurar una impresora o cámara de seguridad, o se quiere comprobar si una red privada virtual (VPN) está ocultando la dirección habitual.
Conocer la dirección IP no requiere instalar programas ni tener conocimientos avanzados de informática. Existen herramientas gratuitas en internet que permiten consultar la dirección pública, mientras que la dirección privada puede encontrarse directamente desde la configuración de una computadora o un teléfono.
¿Qué es una dirección IP y para qué sirve?
La dirección IP, sigla de Internet Protocol (protocolo de internet), es una identificación numérica asignada a un dispositivo cuando se conecta a una red. Su función consiste en permitir que los equipos envíen y reciban información, de manera que los datos puedan llegar al destino correcto.

articles.title: Pile-ins, payouts, and pacing pressure: the investors behind the VCs open up | TechCrunch

The limited partners who provide the capital to venture firms — the “money behind the money” — are feeling great right now. They’re in uncharted territory in many ways, but also potentially exceedingly lucrative territory.
Normally, LPs typically spread their bets across many firms to diversify their own portfolios. They write checks to emerging managers and established ones, to generalist firms and specialists. The goal is a strong return, but also to minimize risk.
That’s the typical playbook. But typical is out the window. OpenAI and Anthropic’s valuations have shot up so quickly that nearly everyone has piled into the same two companies on the way up, often inside the same venture firm, despite the longstanding venture convention of avoiding investments that conflict with one another. No one is complaining, either. The LPs I speak with seem unbothered by this big gamble, given the potential returns; they’re expecting a bonanza.
But they do see danger ahead, even if they describe this as a “yellow light” situation, and they’re uneasy about how quickly VCs are coming back to raise new funds.
I talked about all of it recently with Beezer Clarkson of LGT Capital Partners, a Zurich-based diversified asset manager, and Amit Bhatti of TrueBridge, a Chapel Hill firm that focuses solely on venture. This conversation has been edited for length.

In May 2021, the US Food and Drug Administration released a lengthy briefing document on an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis that often damages the kidneys and lungs. The agency was on the fence about whether to approve the treatment, and it wanted an independent advisory committee to weigh in. Among the questions at hand: Was the drug meaningfully better than existing therapies?
Participants in the study, which had been conducted by the California biotechnology company ChemoCentryx, did appear to have slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year. But according to the FDA, it was hard to interpret the results because the study’s design had been less than optimal. Some advisory committee members expressed a similar view. The effect of the drug, said one, “is just not well verified by this study.”
At the same time, many patients, and some physicians, saw in the data a potentially helpful medication, one that might lessen patients’ reliance on steroids, which are highly effective but often cause severe side effects.
The advisory committee ultimately voted narrowly to recommend approval, and the FDA followed that advice, greenlighting the drug on October 7, 2021. The drug, marketed as Tavneos, started making its way into clinics. A year after approval, ChemoCentryx was acquired by Amgen, one of the world’s largest pharmaceutical companies. Dans celui consacré à la compression, un ouvrier emploie une méthode assez éloignée des algorithmes : il s’assoit sur les fichiers pour les faire tenir dans moins de place. articles.title: How Much Deep Sleep Do You Need? What Sleep Researchers Say Before You Buy a Sleep Tracker - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Two different sleep trackers can read the same night and print two different deep-sleep percentages, and the internet’s reference numbers argue among themselves the same way, with figures from 10 to 25 percent all claiming to be the norm. How much deep sleep you need comes down to one benchmark: healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in deep sleep. The disagreement has a structure, and it takes about five minutes to learn. What follows is the benchmark, why wrist readings of sleep stages wobble, and a five-question check to run before paying for any tracker.
How Much Deep Sleep Do Adults Need? Two Bands Behind the Conflicting Percentages
Two citation bands explain most of the conflict in deep-sleep numbers. Under the AASM staging framework, healthy adults spend about 13 to 23 percent of total sleep in the N3 stage, while 10 to 20 percent is the looser band many sources still quote. A quoted 25 percent usually means retelling inflated the range.
The fix is a two-second reading habit, check the band’s origin before the percentage. AASM staging figures put N3 at 13 to 23 percent of total sleep, commonly cited figures answer with the looser 10 to 20 percent band, and the number 25 percent is what inflated retelling looks like. Results on the high end usually come from sources quoting the wider bands, so the argument never ends until the reader checks which one is in use.

articles.title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
articles.summary:
Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it’s the middle of the night while the clock says it’s lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans.
A new Science study on Manx shearwaters, seabirds that can fly hundreds of kilometers a day over the North Atlantic, shows they jet-lag themselves during their excursions. And because these birds navigate by the Sun, that jet lag leaves a measurable mark—it skews their compass.
Clockwork compass
Patrick Lewin is a behavioral and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford and lead author of the study. “Manx shearwaters are medium-sized birds, about the same size as a pigeon,” Lewin said. “They are white underneath and black on top, but they have very long wings, and they are closely related to albatross.” Manx shearwaters nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic. Most breed around the UK and Ireland, with about half of their population living in Wales.
From there, they head out to feed anywhere from a few dozen to more than 1,000 kilometers into the Atlantic. To get back, shearwaters are thought to work out where they are located using a map sense, possibly based on smells, and then use the Sun as a compass to set their direction.

Beyond the books: Real-time data is driving a small-business lending surge
Small businesses have long treated cash flow management as an afterthought, tallying expenses after the money is gone. Now, financial platforms are folding payments, payroll, credit and lending into one system that can see money moving both ways — and predict where it is headed.
That shift puts software providers in direct competition with banks for small-business credit. articles.title: Why Banks Need Thousands of Test Cycles Before AI Agents Spend Money - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A bank can forgive a chatbot that gives a clumsy answer. It cannot forgive an agent that pays the same invoice twice. As software begins to act on behalf of customers, moving funds and settling bills without a person approving each step, the testing bar rises sharply.
That is why risk teams talk in thousands of test cycles, not dozens. Each cycle replays a payment scenario with small changes, and the goal is to see how the agent behaves when conditions drift. Teams that want a practical picture of how payment infrastructure is assembled and exercised can look at how FinteqHub explains the connections between financial services and technology providers.
What Changes When Software Holds the Wallet
A traditional payment flow has a human checkpoint. Someone clicks, confirms a code, or signs off a batch. An AI agent removes that checkpoint by design, because the whole point is speed and autonomy. Removing the human does not remove the need for judgment. It moves the judgment into rules, limits and monitoring, and every one of those has to be proven before launch.
Why one successful run proves very little
An agent that pays a utility bill correctly on Monday has shown it can handle Monday. Language models are probabilistic, so the same prompt can produce slightly different actions on different runs. Risk officers would rather see forty identical passes than one flawless demo.

NVIDIA runs FP16, BF16, and TF32 tensor math with FP32 accumulation at half rate on GeForce cards, while the same silicon in professional cards runs at full speed. The tool removes that cap before the driver even loads, without any VBIOS flashing. An earlier Windows port from impacifist targeted a single RTX 3090 system, while this one covers all three generations.

The unlock resets on every power-off, so it runs from a USB stick on each cold boot, with Secure Boot disabled or a self-signed certificate enrolled. One potentially company-sinking risk factor, however, does not explicitly appear in the prospectus: diseconomies of scale.
Diseconomies of scale occur when a company’s average cost of producing each unit of output increases as the company grows.
You would think that given the time and effort that Anthropic devoted to ensuring its list of risk factors was complete that they would have included this one. There is a reason, however, that they missed it, despite the fact that diseconomies of scale is the elephant in the room.
We’ve been down this road before with cloud computing. The fundamental economic driver of the hyperscaler clouds was economies of scale: the larger they became, the lower their cost of each unit of output, leading to massive growth and profitability over time.

En réalité, il n’y a aucun vote, seulement une arnaque bien ficelée.
Un faux concours de danse pour pirater votre compte WhatsApp
Tout commence par un message semblant provenir de l’un de vos proches. En réalité, un pirate a pris le contrôle du compte de ce proche et se fait passer pour lui. Le message vous invite à voter pour une jeune fille qui participe à un soi-disant concours de danse. Dans toutes les arnaques de ce type repérées en ligne, les noms Sophie et Eliska sont mobilisés.

En países como Colombia, el 25% de las pymes registró incidentes de phishing, el 20% enfrentó ataques vinculados con vulnerabilidades de software y el 15% tuvo problemas asociados con accesos remotos externos.
A los anteriores riesgos se suman uno menos conocido: las aplicaciones falsas de inteligencia artificial (IA), que buscan instalar programas maliciosos bajo la apariencia de servicios conocidos.
Por qué las empresas pequeñas son un objetivo para los ciberdelincuentes

El tamaño de un negocio no reduce el interés de los ciberdelincuentes. Las pymes suelen manejar datos de clientes, transacciones, contactos de proveedores y archivos operativos que pueden ser utilizados para extorsión, fraude o venta ilegal.

En España hay unas cuantas anomalías fronterizas, como la de Ventorros de Balerma o la eterna pugna entre Teruel y Cuenca por un buen puñado de hectáreas. Pero, de todas ellas, la más alucinante es la que aísla a una villa española en Francia. Parece diseñada para poner a prueba los nervios de un cartógrafo. Llívia es un municipio español en plena Cerdaña francesa, rodeado por completo por Francia y conectado con el resto de España por una carretera que atraviesa suelo francés. No es ningún error del mapa, sino la pura consecuencia de una negociación diplomática del siglo XVII.
La historia suele resumirse así: cuando España tuvo que entregar 33 pueblos de la Cerdaña a Francia, sus negociadores defendieron que Llívia no era un pueblo, sino una villa. Pero lo que aquí interesa es su historia, porque va mucho más allá de una mera negociación.
Una guerra de 24 años. Para entenderlo hay que volver a 1659. España y Francia llevaban desde 1635 enfrentadas en una guerra por la hegemonía europea, que terminó con el Tratado de los Pirineos, firmado en la Isla de los Faisanes, en el Bidasoa. España cedió a Francia el Rosellón y el Conflent, entre otros territorios, pero el trazado en la Cerdaña quedó pendiente porque fronteras históricas, jurisdicciones locales y geografía no encajaban. El tratado encargó a comisarios de ambas coronas decidir qué localidades pasaban a Francia.

articles.title: Veteran Microsoft engineer makes his own RAM from scratch using AI — custom FPGA board dodges extreme 1970s PDP-11 memory prices
articles.summary:
Veteran Microsoft engineer makes his own RAM from scratch using AI — custom FPGA board dodges extreme 1970s PDP-11 memory prices
The times are hard for us all.
Dave Plummer, former Microsoft engineer and wizard of Task Manager, Windows Pinball, and now TMOG, has an interesting project in his hands once again. After seeing exactly how many zeros were in the price tag for a megabyte of memory for his vintage PDP-11, he decided to take matters into his own hands and conjure up a new RAM board.
The PDP-11 is from 1970, and later models could fit in as much as four megabytes of memory. Plummer enlisted the help of ChatGPT and the EasyEDA online circuit simulator, though he notes that he hadn't done complicated projects like this before. As several PDP-11 models used Q-Bus boards for main system components, he designed this RAM as a standalone card, then tested it on a backplane alongside another board containing the system's M8190 CPU.
Atop it, he placed a Lattice MachXO2 FPGA serving as a memory controller (model 2000HC, if you're wondering), connected to four ISSI 1 MB memory chips. After adding a U2S I/O chip, a bank of DIP switches, comm ports, and sprinkling a handful of capacitors, he had a complete circuit. The M8190 board design has a 22-bit bus and reserves the top 256 KB for I/O and ROM.
However, it wasn't a first-time-lucky project. Plummer encountered a few abortive starts, as he'd never flash-programmed an FPGA chip before. He fixed that after a few attempts, but then…

Welcome to clinical AI in 2026
- San Francisco lab Radical Numerics says its Omnii-1 model designed bacteriophages that were given to a patient with a drug-resistant infection, a world first
- The phages were built by rewriting the gene for T7's tail fiber, the protein the virus uses to latch onto bacteria

Radical Numerics has announced its AI-designed viruses (bacteriophages) were given to a sick person, but has not provided much further insight about what happened next.
The San Francisco AI lab announced in October 2026 that bacteriophages designed by its new genome model had been administered to a human patient with an antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection, under a physician-led compassionate-use pathway authorized by the FDA.
If the claim holds, it is the first time an AI-designed organism of any kind has been put into a person as medicine.
Not a new phenomenon, but one that could do with AI assistance

For decades, the semiconductor industry competed on one thing: the individual chip. One of the biggest AI semiconductor industry trends now under way is the shift toward treating chips as components of much larger systems. Performance, cost and reliability are now determined across the package, the rack and the supply chain, not inside a single die.
That shift moves the hardest problems upstream. Packaging, connectivity, yield, sourcing and verification used to come after design, but now they shape it from the first day. AI is shortening development cycles at the same time as it adds to the complexity engineers have to manage. The next phase will be defined by how well companies coordinate across that whole system.
“I think the AI system is our new chips,” said Letizia Giuliano, vice president of product management and marketing at Qualcomm Technologies Inc. “If we were optimizing everything for the silicon in the past, now these days we’re optimizing everything for the system.”
Giuliano and other industry experts spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and co-host Alison Kosik at the GSA Women’s Leadership Initiative event in Palo Alto, California. articles.title: Une taxe sur chaque gigaoctet téléchargé : les députés viennent de voter une mesure qui pourrait coûter cher
articles.summary:
L’Assemblée nationale vient d’adopter un amendement instaurant une taxe de 5,5 centimes sur chaque gigaoctet de données transmis aux internautes français. Si la mesure venait à entrer en vigueur, les fournisseurs de contenus devraient passer à la caisse, avec un risque de répercussion sur le prix de nos abonnements.
Regarder une série sur Netflix, télécharger un jeu vidéo de 100 Go ou simplement passer quelques heures sur YouTube pourrait bientôt coûter plus cher aux plateformes qui nous fournissent ces contenus. Ce vendredi 30 octobre, les députés ont adopté un amendement au projet de loi de finances pour 2027 qui propose de taxer les données circulant sur Internet. Une idée pour le moins originale, défendue au nom d’une meilleure contribution des géants du numérique aux finances publiques. Mais derrière les milliards d’euros espérés par ses auteurs, plusieurs questions se posent, à commencer par celle qui nous intéresse tous : qui finira par payer ?
Une taxe de 5,5 centimes par Go, payée par les plateformes
L’amendement déposé par le député socialiste Laurent Lhardit prévoit la création d’une taxe sur les données numériques envoyées aux internautes français. Le texte a été adopté de justesse, par 11 voix contre 10, malgré l’opposition du gouvernement et du rapporteur général du budget.
Le principe est simple : chaque gigaoctet de données transmis serait taxé à hauteur de 0,055 euro, soit 5,5 centimes.

articles.summary:
Hackers steal $6.3B from Binance in biggest-ever crypto heist
Hackers have stolen about $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance, a major cryptocurrency exchange operator.
The heist is more than four times bigger than the previous largest crypto theft. TRM Labs Inc., a venture-backed blockchain intelligence startup, believes that both cyberattacks were carried out by a North Korean state-backed hacking group tracked as TraderTraitor.
About 40% of the stolen sum comprised stablecoins issued by three major crypto companies: Circle Internet Group Inc., Ripple Labs Inc. and Tether Ltd. They managed to freeze most of the funds before the hackers moved them out of reach. Binance, for its part, has set aside over $6.34 billion to cover users’ losses.
The hackers stole the funds by compromising several of the company’s wallets. One of them powers the infrastructure that Binance uses to process customers’ Ethereum transactions. According to TRM, the hackers breached the wallet late Thursday and sent its entire balance to a wallet they controlled.
TraderTraitor compromised Binance’s wallet by exploiting an Ethereum feature called EIP-7702 that the blockchain’s maintainers released last year. It enables a snippet of code called a smart contract to temporarily control a wallet. EIP-7702 only activates smart contracts if they receive authorization to run from the wallet’s operator. That authorization takes the form of an encrypted message.

Intel shifts production capacity from consumer to server CPUs in face of 'unprecedented' AI demand — company navigating 'one of the most significant supply shortages in history'
Client platforms struggle to get memory anyway, right?
Although the consumer PC market is shrinking and will continue to shrink in the coming quarters, Intel is confident that the overwhelming demand from the AI industry for everything that can compute or store data will offset declines in the client space. To that end, the company is reallocating some of its capacity from client to data center CPUs, expanding its Fab 24 in Ireland to make more Xeons, has begun equipment installation into Fab 62 in Arizona ahead of schedule and vows to make 18A chips there, and is expanding its advanced packaging capacity in New Mexico and Malaysia.
"The industry continues to navigate one of the most significant supply shortages in history, driven by the unprecedented demand for Super Intelligence," said Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, during the company's earnings call. "Against this backdrop, I am pleased by the progress we made growing our server supply in Q3. I am mindful about the ongoing challenges we face in the future quarters to keep pace with server demand."
More Intel 3-based Xeons

articles.title: Como cancelar o Kindle+ (antigo Kindle Unlimited) • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Como cancelar o Kindle+ (antigo Kindle Unlimited)
Assinatura do Kindle Unlimited, agora chamado de Kindle+, pode ser cancelada pelo celular ou computador em poucos passos
Se você deseja cancelar o Kindle Unlimited ou Kindle+, precisará usar o navegador do celular ou do PC para acessar a página de gerenciamento do serviço da Amazon. Se você cansou, precisa parar de pagar ou não vê mais utilidade no Kindle+, siga os passos abaixo para interromper as futuras cobranças mensais da assinatura.
Se você acessou a página de assinaturas da Amazon e não conseguiu encontrar a opção de cancelamento do Kindle Unlimited, pode ser que você tenha feito a adesão pela Play Store do celular.
Nesse caso, você precisará acessar as opções de assinaturas da Play Store e procurar pelo Kindle Unlimited ou Kindle+ entre as inscrições para cancelar o serviço.
Não é possível cancelar o Kindle+ (Kindle Unlimited) pelo próprio dispositivo Kindle ou app de leitura Kindle. Mas você pode usar o próprio celular que tem o aplicativo instalado para fazer o cancelamento usando o navegador.
Sim, mas não instantaneamente. Os livros que você emprestou do Kindle+ ainda ficarão disponíveis durante a vigência da assinatura, ou seja, até a próxima data em que seria feita uma nova cobrança. Após esse período, os livros serão devolvidos automaticamente.
Já os livros comprados individualmente permanecerão na sua biblioteca, independentemente de ter ou não uma assinatura do Kindle+ ativa.

articles.title: Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google, Anthropic and others to support new AI crawling opt-out standard
Google LLC, Microsoft Corp., Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC today announced plans to support an upcoming website crawling standard.
The technology will enable website operators to block artificial intelligence developers from using their content to train their models.
Many websites contain a text file titled “robots.txt” that informs crawlers what content they may access. A publisher can use the file to block scraping across the board or only make specific webpages inaccessible. It’s also possible to include certain other instructions. For example, a company can ask crawlers not to visit its website too often.
Website operators historically used robots.txt files to manage how search engines interact with their properties. Nowadays, the technology also helps regulate the activity of the scrapers with which AI providers collect training data.
A company that wishes to disallow training-related scraping must make multiple edits to its website’s robots.txt file. In particular, it needs to add a separate entry for every single AI provider. If an AI provider uses multiple scrapers to collect data, each scraper requires its own robots.txt entry.
The crawling standard Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI are backing aims to simplify the process. It would allow website operators to block all scrapers that collect training data for generative AI models with a single robots.txt entry. The setting wouldn’t app…

articles.title: 'Online exams are now a waste of time': Top UC Berkeley professor calls time on homework grades as students are increasingly cheating using AI
articles.summary:
'Online exams are now a waste of time': Top UC Berkeley professor calls time on homework grades as students are increasingly cheating using AI
Who did your homework?
- Berkeley professor Richard Borcherds says he no longer grades homework
- The renowned mathematician stated that it is amost impossible to spot a human written submission among those created with AI
- Grading in Borcherds’ classes are now conducted with in-person exams, completed without resorting to electronic devices
Professor Richard Borcherds of the University of California, Berkeley, has revealed he has abandoned grading homework for his math students.
The decision appears to have been made following an improvement in AI-produced homework, which has left educators unable to spot human-penned submissions from those completed using AI.
British-born Borcherds – whose award-winning work includes infinite-dimensional algebras and is currently researching quantum field theory – has determined that his students will be assessed using traditional exams, without reliance on electronic devices.
The decision follows Berkeley’s previous evaluation of AI detection software that it found was unreliable, and prompted the university to allow professors to formulate their own AI policies within the course syllabus.
"Grading for correctness"

articles.title: OpenAI restringirá lo que ChatGPT responde a adolescentes sobre armas, aunque la pregunta parezca inocente
articles.summary:
OpenAI anunció el 30 de octubre que limitará la información sobre armas que ChatGPT entrega a usuarios menores de 18 años, incluso cuando la pregunta parezca inofensiva. La medida forma parte de un paquete de salvaguardas contra la violencia real, que la empresa empezará a aplicar en las próximas semanas.
Según la publicación oficial de la compañía, la versión de ChatGPT para adolescentes restringirá la información práctica sobre armas y sistemas de seguridad que pueda usarse para facilitar actos violentos. El límite rige aunque no haya señales de intención violenta en la conversación.
Las políticas de OpenAI ya prohibían ayudar a cualquier persona a planear o ejecutar actos de violencia, y limitaban la ayuda a adolescentes para conseguir armas. La nueva regla amplía esa protección a datos prácticos que antes no estaban cubiertos.
Los adolescentes podrán seguir usando ChatGPT para prevenir o desescalar la violencia, buscar apoyo y contactar a un adulto de confianza, precisó la empresa.
Cómo decidirá ChatGPT quién es menor de edad
OpenAI dijo que reforzó su sistema de predicción de edad, lanzado el año pasado. El sistema analiza varias señales, como los patrones de comportamiento, para estimar si un usuario es menor de 18 años, y traslada a los adolescentes a la experiencia con más protecciones.

La Marine nationale poursuit le renouvellement de sa flotte de remorqueurs. articles.title: Qué es la ansiedad por inteligencia artificial y por qué preocupa a los expertos
articles.summary:
La ansiedad por la inteligencia artificial se instala en los consultorios de los terapeutas y los datos lo confirman: en una encuesta del Pew Research Center realizada en 2026 a más de 3.400 adultos en Estados Unidos, el 52% de los consultados dijo sentirse más preocupado que entusiasmado por el avance de la IA en la vida cotidiana, frente al 37% que expresó esa misma inquietud en 2021.
El fenómeno tiene nombre propio: ansiedad por IA. Según informó el Washington Post, los especialistas en salud mental advierten que llegó para quedarse. Los miedos van desde perder el trabajo hasta no poder distinguir lo real de lo fabricado por una máquina, y los terapeutas ya tienen respuestas concretas para quienes lo padecen.
La psiquiatra Tracy Foose, terapeuta en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco, lo vivió en carne propia. Cuando empezó a publicar videos en redes sociales, algunos seguidores insistían en que era una influencer generada por computadora, algo que al principio le resultó halagador.
La sensación cambió cuando se puso a investigar. Descubrió que existen múltiples compañías que ofrecen crear dobles digitales capaces de replicar la voz y el rostro de cualquier persona.
“Me di cuenta de que alguien podría hacer un video que se apropiara tan completamente de mi imagen, mi voz, mi cara, que incluso yo podría creer que soy yo”, le dijo al Washington Post. El halago se transformó, según sus propias palabras, en “una forma de terror existencial”.

articles.summary:
Sam Altman says OpenAI won't slow science paper blitz — even though academics are calling it a 'giant bomb'
"It’s really cool and terrible at the same time", say researchers
- OpenAI will keep pushing AI’s scientific discoveries, Sam Altman says
- Some researchers are excited by the ‘fantastic’ breakthroughs
- But others warn that the pace of change is ‘psychologically taxing’
One of the promises that huge AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have made is that their machine learning models will help to solve some of the oldest problems in math and science. The pace of their discoveries has left many experts struggling to keep up, but OpenAI’s Sam Altman just has just said there’s much more in store — and not everyone is happy about that.
Speaking on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman outlined his belief that “Humanity deserves fundamental knowledge, and we should not be sitting on a major fundamental science discovery.”
That rationale is why OpenAI has published breakthrough after breakthrough in these fields, knocking down some of the oldest and toughest problems that have troubled great thinkers for years. But the way in which the company has set out its results has drawn criticism for often inadequate attributions and questionable verification processes.

articles.title: Drones con tecnología láser descubren refugios aborígenes milenarios ocultos en los bosques de Australia
articles.summary:
La protección de testimonios culturales milenarios enfrenta la barrera de la geografía agreste. En vastas regiones del planeta, valiosos sitios arqueológicos permanecen ocultos bajo densos mantos vegetales y precipicios inaccesibles para las búsquedas a pie. Frente a este desafío en Australia, un equipo científico logró identificar tres refugios aborígenes desconocidos mediante drones con tecnología láser en las Montañas Azules.
Este hallazgo marca un avance significativo para la preservación patrimonial, al comprobar que herramientas aéreas avanzadas pueden documentar enclaves históricos resguardados durante milenios por el aislamiento geográfico. Hasta el momento, rastrear estos abrigos rocosos, cavidades naturales en paredes de piedra que funcionaron como resguardo y espacios ceremoniales para las comunidades originarias, dependía de extenuantes caminatas de inspección terrestre.
La topografía accidentada y la densa vegetación de la cordillera impidieron durante décadas un registro sistemático. Aunque el área reúne más de doscientos refugios catalogados con vestigios de ocupación humana, los especialistas calculan que apenas el diez por ciento del territorio ha sido relevado a fondo. Esta limitación mantenía la incógnita sobre la cantidad real de yacimientos y su estado ante factores como la erosión, los incendios y el avance urbano.
El nuevo avance técnico resuelve esta dificultad mediante el uso coordinado de vehículos aéreos no tripulados, análisis informático de datos …

El robots.txt es el archivo donde un sitio indica a los programas que recorren internet qué partes pueden visitar. OpenAI aclaró que la adhesión es voluntaria y que la señal no reemplaza los controles que ya ofrece. Dijo que la aplicará “en los próximos meses” y que dará más detalles cuando lo haga. También instó a otros proveedores de IA a respetarla.

The open-source content-management framework acknowledged that the vulnerability is being "actively exploited in the wild," but provided no specifics about the nature of the activity or the extent of the campaign.

articles.title: AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business

AI vendors are relearning the oldest rule in the data business
Your data could soon be sharpening your competitors' tools
Long before anyone trained a model on customer data, the marketing data business worked out the terms for pooling it. Catalog retailers in the 1990s joined data cooperatives that combined their transaction histories so each member could find new buyers, and the arrangements held together because the rules were blunt.
A retailer contributed data to receive modeled prospects; no member got a rival's customer file; and a company that stopped contributing stopped receiving. Card fraud consortia run on similar give-to-get terms. Nobody would call these systems elegant, but every participant understood the trade.
Software vendors building AI features are now running into the same question, usually without the rules. Traditional software sat on top of a customer's data and operated on it. AI products learn from data, and on a multi-tenant platform, that learning rarely stays within a single account.
One company's records can sharpen the enrichment, lead scoring, and recommendations delivered to thousands of others. A vendor can improve its product for every customer by relying on the work of a few, and most contracts say nothing about whether that trade is fair. The customer still owns its data in any legal sense.
Ownership alone doesn't answer who benefits.

articles.title: Syrian Hacker Behind Fake Tweet That Triggered $136 Billion Market Drop Gets 42 Months in Prison
articles.summary:
Ahmad Umar Agha, a Syrian Electronic Army hacker known online as "Th3Pr0," has been sentenced by a U.S. federal court to 42 months in prison for his role in a hacking conspiracy that targeted Western news outlets.
The conspiracy was organized and led by members of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's inner circle, including the commander of Syria's General Intelligence Directorate, the U.S. Justice Department said on October 29.
The pro-Assad Syrian Electronic Army began its attacks in 2011. Its members sent phishing emails to steal employees' passwords, then used those passwords to deface websites, redirect web traffic, and hijack social media accounts, according to a 2014 FBI affidavit.
On April 23, 2013, the group hijacked the Associated Press's Twitter account and posted a false report that President Barack Obama had been injured in two explosions at the White House.
Twitter's message confirming a password reset for that account was sent to a Gmail account used primarily by Agha, the affidavit says.
The Justice Department said Agha carried out that hack, which caused a temporary $136 billion drop in the value of stocks in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Agha later told Business Insider that a big drop in the Dow "was our goal of that hack attack" and that "it was a big victory for us."
Agha was first charged in June 2014 in a complaint that remained secret until March 2016. That month, the FBI added him and co-defendant Firas Dardar to its Cyber's Most Wanted list …

TeamViewer has fixed a flaw that lets the machine being controlled in a remote session attack the computer that connected to control it. In a TeamViewer session, the computer that connects and takes control is the viewer, and the machine it controls is the host.
A malicious or compromised host can exploit the flaw to crash the viewer's TeamViewer and, depending on the platform, may also run code on the viewer's computer. This works only after the user starts a remote-control session to that host. The fix is in TeamViewer version 15.83.

For this flaw, TeamViewer's bulletin lists the Full Client, Portable, and Android app, but not the Host. The same 15.83 update fixes two other flaws in that bulletin that do affect the Host, so people running the Host should update as well.
Omri Dar, a researcher at security firm Remedio, published a technical account of the flaw on October 29. In this bug, he wrote, "the attacker is the host and the victim is the viewer."

articles.title: The intent compression paradox: How LLM developers are solving semantic erosion to keep human intent alive
articles.summary:
The intent compression paradox: How LLM developers are solving semantic erosion to keep human intent alive
The problem of semantic erosion in LLMs and how developers work around it
As people delegate more abstract reasoning to large language models (LLMs), the precise meaning and nuance of our words can get lost in endless interpretation as LLMs repeatedly process, summarize, and recirculate these words.
Humans aren’t robots that formalize all of their sentences. Instead, we converse with some unwritten cultural and situational tones. For example, in some cultures, asking “Have you eaten yet?” doesn’t literally mean asking if the person has eaten food, but is another polite way of saying “How are you doing?” An LLM may miss this nuance in an essay, interpreting it literally and giving a wrong output.
If AI Model A interprets “Have you eaten yet?” literally, it then passes that same interpretation to Model B, which then passes it to Model C. At the third layer, the nuance gets lost. The AI models provide a coherent output, but one that’s out of the cultural and situational context. This is an example of semantic erosion, where definitional precision and cultural nuance gradually get lost as AI models recirculate interpretations and ideas.
Semantic erosion is a structural error, not a "hallucination" where AI models invent wrong facts. Instead, the output remains clear, but with context stripped away, the meaning changes. It’s a major bottleneck that LLM developers have to work…

articles.title: Cloudflare Reports 18.2 Million Network-Layer DDoS Attacks in Q3, Up 38%
articles.summary:
Threat actors are launching about 8,226 network-layer distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks per hour, Cloudflare revealed Thursday.
The web infrastructure and security company said it autonomously mitigated 18.2 million network-layer (L3) DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests in the third quarter of 2026. That amounts to 197,400 attacks per day, or one attack every 0.44 seconds.
In comparison, a total of 13.2 million and 10.0 million L3 DDoS attacks were recorded in Q2 and Q1 2026, respectively. The increase has been linked to DDoS-for-hire booter or stresser services that are responsible for hundreds of thousands of attacks.
"Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%," the Cloudforce One threat intelligence team said in its quarterly DDoS Threat Report shared with The Hacker News.
An interesting trend is the decline of hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps by 69% from the previous quarter – going from 805 attacks in Q2 to 251 in Q3 – likely as a result of law enforcement actions against AISURU, KimWolf, JackSkid, and Mossad earlier this March.
Still, the threat remains far from completely neutralized, given the emergence of new variants like Dysphoria and Evooo1Bot, Cloudflare warned.
Another notable shift is the decline in Connectionless Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (CLDAP) floods, while DNS amplification jumped 215% to account for 3.43% of all network-layer attacks.

articles.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
articles.summary:
A malicious ChatGPT share link could run an attacker's code in the logged-in session of anyone who opened it, allowing them to read their private conversations, researchers at the security firm Parameter showed.
The researchers reported the flaw through OpenAI's bug bounty program on October 18, and OpenAI fixed it eight days later and rated it P1, its most serious category.
The trap was an ordinary ChatGPT conversation shared via its public link. It could be sent the same way as any real shared chat: by email, as a chat message, as a support ticket, or as a social post.
The victim did not have to install anything, join a workspace, or sign in through the attacker. In the most reliable version of the attack, they opened the link and clicked ChatGPT's Preview button once. In a later version, Parameter set the page to open Preview on its own, so opening the link was the only step.
What the Attacker Could Do
Once the link opened, the attacker's code ran inside the victim's signed-in session with the same access as the real ChatGPT site. It listed the victim's recent conversations, opened a private chat that had never been shared with the attacker, and sent a small portion of it to a server controlled by the researchers.
The code called ChatGPT's own signed-in APIs directly, rather than copying what happened to be on the screen. Because it ran with the victim's full web access, its reach was not limited to those chats. "Essentially, we could perform any action on behalf of the vi…

articles.title: Un entrenamiento breve mejora la detección de rostros creados con IA
articles.summary:
Una capacitación breve que enseña a reconocer patrones generales en los retratos digitales elevó de cerca del 40% al 80% la precisión de los participantes para distinguir caras falsas. El hallazgo, publicado en la revista Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, plantea una alternativa frente a la rapidez con la que evolucionan los generadores de imágenes.
La investigación, difundida por Scientific American, propone alejarse de la búsqueda de errores aislados (como orejas deformes, pupilas duplicadas o accesorios incoherentes) y prestar atención a una impresión más amplia del rostro. Según el estudio, las imágenes creadas por inteligencia artificial suelen reunir rasgos demasiado equilibrados, atractivos y convencionales.
Los errores visibles ya no alcanzan para detectar un rostro artificial
Las primeras herramientas de generación de imágenes dejaban fallas fáciles de identificar. Una piel excesivamente uniforme, una mirada extraña o detalles anatómicos imposibles podían revelar que la foto no correspondía a una persona real. Sin embargo, esos indicios perdieron utilidad a medida que mejoraron los modelos.
Los programas actuales pueden producir retratos capaces de confundir incluso a observadores atentos. La dificultad tiene consecuencias prácticas en entornos digitales donde una foto de perfil puede usarse para fingir una identidad. articles.title: Larry Page, cofundador de Google, se convierte en la tercera persona más rica del mundo y desplaza a Michael Dell
articles.summary:
El cofundador de Google, Larry Page, alcanzó el tercer puesto entre las personas más ricas del planeta después de superar a Michael Dell, fundador de Dell Technologies. El cambio se produjo tras una fuerte caída de las acciones de la compañía informática, que redujo en 17.500 millones de dólares el patrimonio de su principal accionista, según las estimaciones en tiempo real de Forbes.
Alrededor del mediodía del viernes, la fortuna de Page se estimaba en 234.400 millones de dólares, mientras que la de Dell había descendido a 229.200 millones. La diferencia de 5.200 millones de dólares permitió que el empresario vinculado a Google avanzara en el ranking internacional de multimillonarios.
El movimiento ocurrió en una jornada marcada por las pérdidas de las principales compañías tecnológicas en Wall Street. Los inversores reaccionaron a los resultados financieros de Intel y a las perspectivas del mercado de computadoras personales, además de expresar preocupación por el elevado gasto que las empresas están destinando al desarrollo de inteligencia artificial.
Aunque Page consiguió avanzar en la clasificación, su patrimonio también registró una reducción durante la jornada. Su fortuna cayó aproximadamente 1.500 millones de dólares, debido principalmente a la pérdida de valor de las acciones de Alphabet, la empresa matriz de Google.
La situación se produjo después de que los títulos de Alphabet retrocedieran un 12% en la jornada anterior, tras la publicación de sus resultados corres…

articles.title: Alphabet apuesta por los robotaxis de Waymo, pero el negocio todavía representa menos del 1% de sus ingresos
articles.summary:
Alphabet registró ingresos por 127.600 millones de dólares durante el tercer trimestre de 2026, pero una de sus divisiones tuvo resultados muy diferentes. Other Bets, el segmento que incluye a Waymo, su negocio de vehículos autónomos, generó 372 millones de dólares en ventas y registró pérdidas operativas por 2.050 millones de dólares entre julio y septiembre.
Los resultados muestran la diferencia entre el tamaño de los negocios principales de Alphabet y el de sus proyectos experimentales. Mientras Google Services y Google Cloud concentran la mayor parte de los ingresos de la compañía, Waymo continúa ampliando sus operaciones de transporte sin conductor y prepara su llegada a nuevos mercados internacionales, entre ellos Londres y Tokio.
La división Other Bets representa aproximadamente el 0,29% de los ingresos trimestrales de Alphabet. Su facturación aumentó un 8% frente al mismo período del año anterior, cuando había registrado 343 millones de dólares. Sin embargo, sus pérdidas operativas también crecieron: pasaron de 1.430 millones a 2.050 millones de dólares.
Waymo busca expandirse a Londres y Tokio
Waymo es uno de los proyectos más importantes de Alphabet fuera de sus negocios tradicionales. La compañía desarrolla vehículos autónomos que ofrecen servicios de transporte sin conductor y actualmente opera en 15 ciudades de Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Présidentielle 2027 : ce que les réseaux sociaux peuvent vraiment changer, de la méthode de Lula aux blocages d’internautes
articles.summary:
Plus de 10 millions d'abonnés recevaient sur WhatsApp les consignes du député André Janones le jour de la réélection de Lula. Des internautes français ont repris sa méthode à l'approche de la présidentielle de 2027, et déclarent par millions des blocages de comptes d'extrême droite sans savoir ce que ce geste change pour les algorithmes.
Lula a remporté le second tour de la présidentielle brésilienne le 25 octobre, avec 51,8 % des voix contre Flávio Bolsonaro. André Janones confiait chaque jour des « missions » aux abonnés de sa chaîne « Exército do Lula », passés d'environ 50 000 avant le premier tour à plus de 10 millions. Ils devaient relayer les vidéos favorables au président sortant et laisser sans réponse les publications de ses adversaires.
Rien ne permet d'affirmer que cette armée numérique a fait gagner Lula, mais des internautes français ont adapté sa méthode en quelques jours, après plusieurs semaines de blocus lycéens et deux journées de manifestations, les 17 et 24 octobre. À l'heure où on écrit cet article et que l'acte III du mouvement citoyen en France continue, les citoyens peuvent-ils vraiment peser sur la vie politique depuis leur téléphone, quand les plateformes décident en grande partie de qui verra leurs messages ?

articles.title: Le patron d’OVHcloud fait les comptes, la taxe sur les gigaoctets coûterait un montant colossal à son entreprise
articles.summary:
Le fondateur d’OVHcloud, Octave Klaba, a calculé samedi l’impact de la taxe sur les gigaoctets votée par les députés. Il a chiffré jusqu'à 70 millions d'euros ce que l'hébergeur français pourrait devoir chaque année au fisc.
Au lendemain du vote de la taxe sur les gigaoctets dans une Assemblée nationale qui ressemblait davantage à une cathédrale en pleine nuit, au vu du faible nombre de participants, Octave Klaba, le fondateur et PDG d'OVHcloud, a sorti sa calculette. Dans un long message publié ce samedi 31 octobre, où il invite même ses lecteurs à le corriger, il compare les 5,5 centimes prévus par l'amendement I-1358 au prix réel de la bande passante, avant d'estimer ce que son entreprise devrait verser. Une démonstration chiffrée qui, en cette journée particulière, n'est pas destinée à faire peur mais qui donne corps aux craintes d'un effet boomerang pour le cloud français.
Une taxe au gigaoctet plus chère que la bande passante elle-même
Sur le papier, les 0,055 euro par gigaoctet votés vendredi par 11 voix contre 10 semblent anodins. Après tout, on ne parle que de 5 centimes, non ? Évidemment, c'est un peu plus compliqué que ça. Octave Klaba évoque un chiffre « abstrait » et le confronte au prix de gros d'Internet. Il prend l'exemple d'un port à 100 Gbit/s, l'équivalent d'un gros tuyau réseau.
